definition_zh: 法律（总称）；一条法律；定律；规则；执法机构；法学
definition_en: a rule that a community accepts as binding, or the whole system of such rules, or a regular pattern in nature
core_image: 石柱上刻着一排条文，旁边站着执法的人，远处实验室的黑板上写着另一条「定律」
scene: 公告栏上钉着新条文，摊主们围着读，谁也没先开口。 The new law reaches every stall in the market.
sceneCN: 这里 law 指正式颁行的一条法律（第 2 个义项：一部法律）；句意为这条新法律管到市场上的每一个摊位。

pos.zh: （口语，用定冠词）执法机构；警方

derivatives.zh: 合法的（law + -ful「充满」，由法律转指符合其要求）
无法无天的（law + -less「无」，由法律转指其缺失）
律师（law + -yer「从事者」，由法律转指以此为业的人）
亡命之徒；宣布非法（out「在外」+ law，由法律转指被逐出法外）

senses.title: The system of rules
senses.definition: the whole body of binding rules of a community, seen as one system
senses.definitionCN: 某一社群全部有约束力的规则，被视为一个体系
senses.example: Law is slow, but it remembers.
senses.exampleCN: 法律很慢，但它记得住。
senses.why: the mass-noun use is the oldest general sense: law as an institution rather than a list of items.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法是最古老的泛指义：法作为制度，而非条目清单。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted rule with a number, a date and an issuing body
senses.definitionCN: 带编号、日期与颁行机关的单条规则
senses.example: The new law reaches every stall in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新法律管到市场上的每一个摊位。
senses.why: English made law countable so that individual acts could be cited and dated.
senses.whyCN: 英语让 law 可数，以便单条法令可被引用与记年。

senses.title: A regularity of nature
senses.definition: a statement that a natural process always behaves in a specified way
senses.definitionCN: 断言某一自然过程总以特定方式进行的陈述
senses.example: The law holds far from the laboratory as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这条定律在实验室之外也成立。
senses.why: the seventeenth century extended the word from decrees to regularities, since both are rules that cannot be broken.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪把这个词从法令扩展到规律，因为两者都是不可违反的规则。

senses.title: A rule of a game or body
senses.titleCN: 比赛或机构内部的规则
senses.definition: an agreed rule governing play, a society or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 约定管辖比赛、社团或机构的规则
senses.example: The law of the club is older than the clubhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部的规则比会所还老。
senses.why: any self-governing body reproduces the statute model, so the word follows the rule wherever it binds.
senses.whyCN: 任何自治团体都会复制法令的模式，于是这个词跟着规则走到哪里绑到哪里。

senses.title: The police, in speech
senses.definition: the police or the enforcement arm, used with the definite article
senses.definitionCN: 警察或执法部门，惯用定冠词
senses.example: The law arrived twenty minutes after the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 警笛响过二十分钟后警察就到了。
senses.why: metonymy names the enforcers by the thing they enforce, an old colloquial habit.
senses.whyCN: 转喻用所执行之物来称呼执行者，是古老的口语习惯。

senses.title: The study and profession
senses.definition: the academic discipline of law and the profession that practises it
senses.definitionCN: 研究法律的学科以及以此执业的行业
senses.example: She read law before joining the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她入部之前读的是法律。
senses.why: a body of rules large enough to need specialists becomes a discipline and a career.
senses.whyCN: 规则多到需要专家时，便成为一门学科与一种职业。

senses.title: A governing principle
senses.definition: a principle that explains how a domain works, as in the law of supply and demand
senses.definitionCN: 解释某一领域如何运作的原理，如供需法则
senses.example: The law of supply and demand explains the queue, not the price.
senses.exampleCN: 供需法则解释的是排队，不是价格。
senses.why: economics borrowed the prestige of natural law to describe tendencies that hold on average.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借来自然法的威望，用来描述平均成立的趋势。

senses.title: An inescapable rule
senses.definition: a rule presented as unavoidable, as in the law of the jungle
senses.definitionCN: 被说成不可避免的规则，如丛林法则
senses.example: The law of the jungle returned when the patrols stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻一停，丛林法则就回来了。
senses.why: the figurative use keeps the binding force and drops the institution, leaving only inevitability.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法保留了约束力而丢掉机构，只剩不可避免。

intro.en: Law comes from Old English lagu, itself borrowed from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', from leggja 'to lay'. It has no Latin source, unlike legal and legislation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: law 来自古英语 lagu，而 lagu 借自古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」，出自 leggja「放置」。与 legal、legislation 不同，它没有拉丁来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lag meant 'something laid down, a layer, a fixed order', from the verb leggja 'to lay'. The image is a rule placed down where people can see it.
items.cn: lag 意为「被放下之物、层次、既定秩序」，出自动词 leggja「放置」。意象是被放在人们看得见之处的规则。

items.en: Old English borrowed lagu from Norse during the Viking period; the native word for divine law was ǣ, which later dropped out.
items.cn: 古英语在维京时期从诺斯语借入 lagu；本土表示神法的词是 ǣ，后来消失。

items.en: Lagu settled into Middle English as lawe, taking over the general sense of binding custom and statute.
items.cn: lagu 进入中古英语作 lawe，接管了有约束力的习俗与法令这一泛义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century law was applied to regularities of nature, so that a falling apple and a statute shared one word.
items.cn: 17 世纪起 law 被用于自然规律，于是落下的苹果与一条法令共用同一个词。

items.en: Legal, legitimate and legislation descend from Latin lex, not from lagu; the resemblance is in meaning only, and the two families are unrelated at the root.
items.cn: legal、legitimate、legislation 上溯拉丁 lex，而非 lagu；相似只在意义上，两个词族在词根上并无关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Norse origin of lag is not established, and the relation sometimes proposed between lag and the English verb lay is plausible but not demonstrated as a direct derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：lag 在诺斯语之前的来源未得到证明；有人提出 lag 与英语动词 lay 的关系，看似合理，却未被证明为直接派生。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look related to law but come from Latin lex; group two holds near neighbours in the legal field.
note.cn: 第一组是看着与 law 有关、实际来自拉丁 lex 的词；第二组是法律领域的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin legalis, built on lex; it means permitted by law, not the law itself, and is unrelated at the root to law.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legalis，由 lex 构成；意为法律允许的，而非法律本身，与 law 在词根上无关。

entries.definition: The making of laws, from lex and latus; it names the process, not the Norse-rooted body of rules.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律，来自 lex 与 latus；指过程，而非那个诺斯语词根的规则总体。

entries.definition: law plus -ful: conforming to the rules, an adjective built on the native noun.
entries.definitionCN: law 加 -ful：符合规则的，是本族名词派生的形容词。

entries.definition: Out 'outside' plus law: one placed outside the law's protection, so the root is kept and reversed.
entries.definitionCN: out「在外」加 law：被置于法律保护之外的人，词根保留而意义反转。

entries.definition: A formal written law passed by a legislature; law is the wider word that also covers custom and case law.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的正式成文法；law 是更宽的说法，也涵盖习惯法与判例法。

entries.definition: A regulation of an activity or a game; law implies a community's binding authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 某项活动或比赛的规章；law 暗含社群约束性权威在其背后。

entries.definition: A rule issued by an agency under a statute; it is law in a derived, technical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的规则；在派生、技术的意义上也是法。

entries.definition: A general truth that explains workings; it matches the scientific sense of law without any authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 解释运作的一般真理；对应 law 的科学义，背后却没有权威。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old Norse lag 'something laid down': a rule is a thing placed where all can see it.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」：规则就是放在人人看得见之处的东西。

normal.en: The family runs lawful, lawless, lawyer, outlaw, by-law.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lawful、lawless、lawyer、outlaw、by-law。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: break the law, by law, the rule of law, a law of nature.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出义项：违法、依法、法治、自然定律。

normal.en: Two senses share one word: the statute in the book and the regularity on the blackboard.
normal.cn: 两个义项共用一个词：书里的法令与黑板上的规律。

normal.en: Keep legal apart: it comes from Latin lex, so its resemblance to law is meaning, not blood.
normal.cn: 把 legal 分开放：它来自拉丁 lex，与 law 的相似是意义上的，不是血缘上的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone with lines cut into it, standing where everyone walks past.
abstract.cn: 想象一块刻着横线的石头，立在人人都经过的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that keeps working after the person who wrote it is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则，写它的人不在了，它还在运作。

abstract.en: Picture two blackboards, one with a statute, one with an equation, both called law.
abstract.cn: 想象两块黑板，一块写着法令，一块写着方程，都叫 law。

examples.en: The law requires the seller to name the origin of the goods.
examples.cn: 法律要求卖方标明货物的产地。

examples.en: By law, the minutes must be public within a month.
examples.cn: 依法，会议记录必须在一个月内公开。

examples.en: The law of demand fails when buyers cannot compare prices.
examples.cn: 当买方无法比较价格时，需求法则就失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: law＝「放下的东西」：一条条放在那里、谁都得照着走；记「书里有条文，黑板上有定律」。

root: 古英语 lagu ← 古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」← leggja「放置」；lag 在诺斯语之前的来源不确定，与英语 lay 的关系仅为合理推测。与拉丁 lex 词族（legal、legislation）无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one laid-down rule: the system, a single act, a regularity of nature, a game rule, the police, the profession, an economic principle, and an unavoidable rule of the jungle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一条被放下的规则散开：体系、单条法令、自然规律、比赛规则、警方、法律职业、经济原理，以及丛林里的必然规矩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rule laid down in public, heavy enough that people arrange their days around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条当众放下的规则，重到人们要围着它安排日子。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND UNIT: the whole body of rules, then one dated item inside it.
branches.cn: 体系与单位：规则总体，以及其中一条记年的条目。

branches.en: RULES WITHOUT A LAWGIVER: nature and the market exhibit regularities that cannot be disobeyed.
branches.cn: 没有立法者的规则：自然与市场呈现不可违背的规律。

branches.en: SMALL SCALES OF BINDING: a club's rulebook, and the jungle's unavoidable order.
branches.cn: 约束的小尺度：俱乐部的规则手册，以及丛林的必然秩序。

branches.en: THE ENFORCERS: the police named by what they enforce.
branches.cn: 执行者：用所执行之物来称呼警察。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: a body of rules large enough to become a career.
branches.cn: 学科：规则多到足以成为一种职业。

intro.en: Law is a Norse loanword, so its family is built with English suffixes rather than Latin ones, unlike legal and legislation.
intro.cn: law 是诺斯语借词，因此其词族由英语后缀而非拉丁后缀构成，这一点与 legal、legislation 不同。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin entry here: the Latin lex family supplies legal and legislation but is not related to law at the root.
latinIntro.cn: 此处没有拉丁条目：拉丁 lex 词族给出 legal 与 legislation，但与 law 在词根上无关。

items.meaning: a binding rule; the body of such rules
items.meaningCN: 有约束力的规则；此类规则的总体
items.example: The law was read from the steps.
The search was lawful but rude.
The port grew lawless after the garrison left.
items.exampleCN: 驻军撤走后港口变得无法无天。

items.example: Her lawyer read the clause twice.
items.exampleCN: 她的律师把条款读了两遍。

items.meaning: one put outside the law; to ban
items.meaningCN: 被置于法外者；宣布非法
items.example: The practice was outlawed in the last session.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法在上个会期被宣布非法。

items.example: The by-law limits noise after ten.
items.exampleCN: 该细则限制十点后的噪音。

items.example: The legality of the order was disputed.
items.exampleCN: 这道命令的合法性受到质疑。

definition_zh: 医院；住院处
definition_en: a place where sick or injured people are given medical treatment by doctors and nurses
core_image: 挂着白床单的安静走廊：白天有人推着轮椅经过，夜里只剩仪器的小灯
scene: 放学路过街角，救护车正停在诊所隔壁的大白楼前。 Grandma stayed in the hospital for a week after her fall.
sceneCN: 这里 hospital 是「医院」（第 1 个义项：治病的地方）；奶奶摔倒后在那里住了一周。

collocations.zh: 去医院（看病；英式指住院）

derivatives.zh: hospital + -ity → 好客；殷勤招待（同根词，源于「接待客人」）
hospital + -able → 好客的；热情接待的
同根词 → 主人；主持人（接待者）
同根词 → 青年旅舍；招待所

senses.title: A place for treating the sick
senses.definition: a building where doctors and nurses treat sick or injured people
senses.definitionCN: 医生护士为病人和伤者治疗的建筑
senses.example: The new hospital has a large garden for patients.
senses.exampleCN: 新医院有一个供病人休养的大花园。
senses.why: The core sense is the house that receives those who cannot stay home.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是「接待无法留在家中的人的那栋房子」。

senses.title: Being a patient there
senses.definition: the time a person spends in hospital as a patient
senses.definitionCN: 一个人作为病人在医院度过的时段
senses.example: His hospital after the accident lasted almost a month.
senses.exampleCN: 事故后他住院将近一个月。
senses.why: English uses the building’s name for the stay itself: in hospital means inside its care.
senses.whyCN: 英语用建筑名指住院本身：in hospital 即「处于它的照护之中」。

senses.title: A charitable institution in history
senses.definition: in older use, a house that gave care and shelter to the poor, old or travellers
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指收容照顾穷人、老人或旅者的机构
senses.example: An old hospital for travellers stood by the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 山道旁曾有一座收留旅者的慈善院。
senses.why: Before modern medicine, the word meant any house of care, not only a place for the sick.
senses.whyCN: 在现代医学出现之前，该词泛指任何提供照护的房子，不只为病人服务。

intro.en: Hospital comes from Latin hospitalis, of a guest, from hospes, meaning guest and host at once.
intro.cn: hospital 来自拉丁 hospitalis「客人的」，其词根 hospes 同时表示「客人」与「主人」。

items.en: Latin hospes meant both guest and host: the one received and the one receiving.
items.cn: 拉丁 hospes 兼指客人与主人：被接待者与接待者。

items.en: The adjective hospitalis meant of a guest or of hospitality; the noun hospitalia meant guest rooms.
items.cn: 形容词 hospitalis 意为「与客人有关的」，名词 hospitalia 指客房。

items.en: Old French hospital named houses run by the Church to shelter the poor and the sick.
items.cn: 古法语 hospital 指教会开办、收容贫病者的院舍。

items.en: Middle English borrowed hospital in the thirteenth century with this charitable sense.
items.cn: 中古英语十三世纪借入 hospital，取其慈善义。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the word to medical care, while the old guest sense survives in host, hostel and hospitality.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义收窄到医疗，古老的「待客」义留在 host、hostel、hospitality 中。

note.en: Group one holds the Latin guest family; group two holds places connected with healing.
note.cn: 第一组是拉丁「客人」词族；第二组是与医治相关的场所词。

entries.definition: a cheap place for travellers to sleep
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「旅舍」，保留待客旧义

entries.definition: friendly welcome given to guests
kind and welcoming to guests
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「好客的」

entries.definition: a small place for medical advice and treatment, not for staying
a large room in a hospital with several beds
a place for long rest and treatment

normalIntro.en: Use the guest root family to build the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用「客人」词根家族来建这个词。

normal.en: hospes means guest and host: a hospital hosts its guests
normal.cn: hospes 兼指客人与主人：医院就是接待「客人」的主人家。

normal.en: hospital + -ity = hospitality, welcoming guests warmly
normal.cn: hospital + -ity＝hospitality，热情待客。

normal.en: host, hostel, hospital all grew from one Latin root
normal.cn: host、hostel、hospital 都长自同一拉丁词根。

normal.en: in hospital without the: British English means as a patient
normal.cn: 英式英语说 in hospital 不加 the：作为病人在住院。

normal.en: children’s hospital: the hospital for children
normal.cn: children’s hospital＝儿童医院。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway that never closes: anyone carried in is received.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇从不关上的门：被抬进来的人都会被接待。

abstract.en: Picture rows of beds, each one with its own small light.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排病床，每张床亮着一盏小灯。

abstract.en: Feel the quiet of a ward after ten at night.
abstract.cn: 感受晚上十点后病房的安静。

examples.en: The injured player was taken to hospital at once.
examples.cn: 受伤的球员被立刻送往医院。

examples.en: She visits her uncle in hospital every Sunday.
examples.cn: 她每周日去探望住院的叔叔。

examples.en: The town built a new children’s hospital last year.
examples.cn: 镇上去年新建了一座儿童医院。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好死皮特」——好心的皮特开诊所收留病人，那栋白楼就是 hospital（医院）。

root: hospital 来自拉丁 hospitalis「与客人有关的」，词根 hospes 兼指客人、主人；同根词有 host、hostel、hospitality，均保留「接待」的古义。

sensesIntro.en: From a house that receives guests, hospital narrowed to the house that receives the sick.
sensesIntro.cn: hospital 从「接待客人的房子」收窄为「接待病人的房子」，住院义由建筑名引申而来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house that receives those who cannot stay home
core.cn: 核心意象：收留无法留在家中者的那栋房子

branches.en: the building of medical care
branches.cn: 实施医疗的建筑（义项 01）

branches.en: the stay inside its care
branches.cn: 处在它照护下的时段（义项 02）

branches.en: the older shelter for anyone in need
branches.cn: 旧时收容一切的院舍（义项 03）

branches.en: care first, medicine later
branches.cn: 先有照护，后有医学（义项 01 · 03）

branches.en: the building name stands for the stay
branches.cn: 建筑名代指住院本身（义项 01 · 02）

intro.en: Hospital belongs to the Latin guest family, one of the most productive roots in English.
intro.cn: hospital 属于拉丁「客人」词族，是英语里能产性最高的词根之一。

latinIntro.en: Latin hospes, hospit-, guest and host, is the true ancestor of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 hospes（词干 hospit-，客人、主人）是整个词族的真正祖先。

items.example: Hospes carries both roles in one word.
items.exampleCN: hospes 一个词兼含两种角色。

items.meaning: a house of care for the sick
items.example: The hospital opened a new ward.
Their hospitality was famous in the town.
items.exampleCN: 他们的好客在镇上出名。

items.example: The host poured tea for everyone.
They stayed in a youth hostel.
Also gives hostile, originally of strangers.
items.exampleCN: 还派生 hostile，本义与陌生人有关。

definition_zh: 黄油；涂黄油于；（口语）奉承、讨好
definition_en: a soft yellow food made from cream and spread on bread, to spread it on food, or in informal speech to flatter someone
core_image: 一块淡黄色、表面带刀痕的黄油放在面包旁
scene: 早餐桌上，她把一小块黄油抹在刚烤好的吐司上。 She spread butter on the warm toast.

senses.title: The yellow food from cream
senses.definition: a soft yellow food made from cream, spread on bread or used in cooking
senses.definitionCN: 用奶油制成的淡黄色软食，涂在面包上或用于烹饪
senses.example: She spread butter on the warm toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她把黄油抹在温热的吐司上。
senses.why: The word travelled from Greek through Latin, where boutyron literally meant cow cheese.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从希腊语经由拉丁语传来，其中 boutyron 字面意思就是「牛的奶酪」。

senses.title: To spread butter on
senses.definition: to put butter on bread or another food
senses.definitionCN: 把黄油涂在面包或其他食物上
senses.example: Butter the pan before you add the eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 打鸡蛋之前先在锅里抹一层黄油。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the everyday act of spreading it.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，用来指抹黄油这个日常动作。

senses.title: To flatter someone
senses.definition: to flatter someone so that they will help you, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指奉承某人，好让对方帮自己
senses.example: He tried to butter up the teacher before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前他试着讨好老师。
senses.why: Soft butter spreads easily, and smooth flattery spreads over a person the same way.
senses.whyCN: 软黄油很容易抹开，顺耳的奉承也以同样的方式铺到人身上。

intro.en: Butter came into English from Latin, which had taken it from Greek, and the Greek word meant cow cheese.
intro.cn: butter 从拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语又是从希腊语借来的，希腊语原词意为「牛的奶酪」。

items.en: Boutyron joined bous, cow, with tyros, cheese.
items.cn: boutyron 把 bous（牛）与 tyros（奶酪）组合在一起。

items.en: Latin took the word as butyrum and used it for the yellow fat.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 butyrum，用来指这种黄色的油脂。

items.en: Old English borrowed butere, most likely through church and kitchen Latin.
items.cn: 古英语借入 butere，很可能经由教会与厨房使用的拉丁语。

items.en: German Butter and Dutch boter show the same borrowed word across the north.
items.cn: 德语 Butter 与荷兰语 boter 显示这个词在北方各地同样被借用。

items.en: Today butter is a food, a verb and, in slang, a way of flattering.
items.cn: 今天 butter 是食物、动词，俚语中还指奉承。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects dairy foods.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收乳制品。

definition_zh: 代理人；经纪人；特工；作用剂
definition_en: a person who acts for another, or a thing that produces an effect
core_image: 一位经纪人在电话里替客户谈生意
scene: 办公室里，一位经纪人正在电话中替客户洽谈。 The agent sold the house for us.
sceneCN: 这里 agent 是「代理人」（第 1 个义项：替别人办事的人）；句意为这位代理人替我们卖掉了房子。

senses.title: A person who acts for another
senses.definition: a person who does business for someone else
senses.definitionCN: 替别人办事的人
senses.example: The agent sold the flat for the owner.
senses.exampleCN: 代理人替房主卖掉了公寓。
senses.why: Agent comes from Latin agere, to do, so an agent is simply a person who does something for another.
senses.whyCN: agent 来自拉丁语 agere「做」，替别人做事的人就是代理人。

senses.title: A person who manages work
senses.definition: a person who finds work or deals for an actor or a player
senses.definitionCN: 为演员或选手找机会、谈事务的人
senses.example: Her agent found her a role in a film.
senses.exampleCN: 她的经纪人替她找到电影角色。
senses.why: In films and sport, the person who does the dealing for a performer is an agent.
senses.whyCN: 在影视与体育里替表演者谈事务的人，就是经纪人。

senses.title: A force that causes change
senses.definition: a thing that produces an effect
senses.definitionCN: 产生某种作用的事物
senses.example: Wind is an agent of change in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 风是沙漠中促成变化的因素。
senses.why: The doing was widened to any force that acts, which gives the sense of a factor.
senses.whyCN: 把「起作用者」扩到任何产生作用的力量，就是因素。

senses.title: A secret worker for a state
senses.definition: a person who works secretly for a government
senses.definitionCN: 为政府秘密工作的人
senses.example: The agent carried a small radio.
senses.exampleCN: 那名特工带着一台小收音机。
senses.why: A person who acts secretly for a state is the modern sense of a secret agent.
senses.whyCN: 为国家秘密做事的人，就是现代意义的特工。

senses.example: Let us begin.
senses.exampleCN: 我们开始吧。
senses.why: The speaker opens a door for shared action, so the verb frames proposals.
senses.whyCN: 说话者为共同行动开一扇门，动词于是构成提议框架。

senses.title: To rent out
senses.definition: to allow someone to use a house or room in return for rent
senses.definitionCN: 允许他人在付费条件下使用房屋或房间
senses.example: They let the flat to two students.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把公寓租给两名学生。
senses.why: Use is granted for a price, so permission extends to property.
senses.whyCN: 使用权被有偿授予，允许便延伸到房产。

senses.title: To allow through
senses.definition: to allow someone or something to pass or enter
senses.definitionCN: 允许人或物通过或进入
senses.example: The guard let the trucks through.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵放行了卡车。
senses.why: A barrier lowers and traffic flows: letting is opening the way.
senses.whyCN: 栏杆抬起，车流通过：放行就是开路。

senses.title: To release or stop holding
senses.definition: to stop holding or confining something
senses.definitionCN: 停止握住或关住某物
senses.example: Let go of the rope slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢松开绳子。
senses.why: The grip opens and the thing is free, the plainest picture of permission.
senses.whyCN: 松手即自由，这是「允许」最直白的画面。

senses.title: To become weaker (let up)
senses.definition: to become less strong or stop, as rain or effort
senses.definitionCN: （雨势或努力）变弱或停止
senses.example: The rain finally let up at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 雨到中午终于小了。
senses.why: Pressure relaxes as if it were a hand that stops gripping.
senses.whyCN: 压力松弛，仿佛一只不再紧握的手。

intro.en: Let comes from Old English laetan "to allow, leave", from Germanic laetan, from a root meaning "to leave, let go"; the rental sense grew from granting use.
intro.cn: let 来自古英语 laetan「允许、留下」，出自日耳曼语 laetan，词根意为「离开、放开」；出租义由「授以使用权」发展而来。

items.en: Old English laetan meant 'to allow, let go, leave', already covering release and permission.
items.cn: 古英语 laetan 意为「允许、放开、留下」，已含释放与许可两义。

items.en: Germanic laetan ties the verb to a root of leaving and loosening, kin to the family of late and last.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 laetan 把动词系于「离开、松弛」词根，与 late、last 词族有亲缘。

items.en: In Middle English let developed the legal rental sense as land tenure spread.
items.cn: 中古英语随土地租佃普及，let 发展出法定的出租义。

items.en: Modern English kept the imperative let for suggestions, and tennis borrowed let for a replayed serve.
items.cn: 现代英语保留祈使 let 用于建议；网球借 let 指「擦网球重发」。

items.en: Norse influence may have reinforced the letting and hindering shades in northern dialects.
items.cn: 诺斯语影响可能强化了北方方言里「允许」与「妨碍」的色彩。

note.cn: 第一组标出形近词；第二组列出许可与松放之词。

To let go of something held or confined.
To pay for use; the user\u2019s side of letting.
entries.definitionCN: 付费使用；出租中使用者的一侧。

abstract.cn: 想象手不再抵着，门自己荡开。

abstract.en: Picture rain easing until the umbrella folds shut.
abstract.cn: 想象雨渐弱，伞终于收拢。

abstract.en: Picture a held bird freed when fingers uncurl.
abstract.cn: 想象手指张开，握着的鸟飞走。

definition_zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金
definition_en: a small bag used for carrying money, especially a woman's handbag; also the money a person or group has available, or the prize money offered in a competition
core_image: 围裙内袋里一只磨旧的皮钱袋，装着一整天的收入
scene: 早市快收摊时，卖菜的女人把零钱一张张理平，塞进围裙内侧的布袋。 She kept the day's takings in a worn leather purse.
sceneCN: 这里 purse 是「钱包、随身钱袋」（第 1 个义项：装钱的小包）；句意为她把一天的收入放进一只磨旧的皮钱包里。画面里可留意：围裙、理平的零钱、旧皮袋。

pos.zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金

derivatives.zh: purse 加表人后缀 -er，原指管钱袋的人，现指船上掌管账目与薪水的职务

purse 与 proud 复合，指因富有而傲慢的

senses.title: A small bag for carrying money
senses.definition: a small bag, often with a clasp, used especially by women for carrying money and a few personal items
senses.definitionCN: 尤指女性使用、常带扣合的小包，用来装钱和少量随身物品
senses.example: She took a coin from her purse and paid the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 她从钱包里取出一枚硬币付给司机。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it named a leather bag, and the first English purses were soft pouches pulled shut with strings, long before notes and cards existed.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁词本指皮袋，英语最早的 purse 就是用细绳收口的小软袋，那时还没有纸币和银行卡。

senses.title: The money a person or group can spend
senses.definition: the amount of money that a person, family or organization has available to spend
senses.definitionCN: 个人、家庭或机构手头可供支配的钱
senses.example: The repair cost more than the family purse could bear.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔修缮费超出了这个家庭的财力。
senses.why: Once a container holds money, the container can stand for the contents, and then for the spending power those contents give.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦装着钱，就能代指里面的钱，再进一步指这些钱带来的购买力。

senses.title: Prize money in a competition
senses.definition: the sum of money offered as a prize in a race, a fight or another contest
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑、拳赛或其他比赛中作为奖品的钱
senses.example: The boxer gave his purse to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 这名拳手把奖金捐给了村里的学校。
senses.why: Prize money was once handed over in an actual bag at the end of a contest, so the name of the container stayed on the prize after payments moved to cheques.
senses.whyCN: 比赛结束时奖金真的装在一只袋子里当场交付，所以即使后来改用支票，容器之名仍留在奖金上。

intro.en: Purse travels back through Old French and medieval Latin to Latin bursa, a leather bag; the Greek word behind bursa is generally thought to be a borrowing, so anything deeper is uncertain.
intro.cn: purse 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语 bursa（皮袋）；bursa 背后的希腊词一般认为也是借词，再往前的来源并不确定。

items.en: Greek byrsa meant a hide or a leather bag, and it is generally considered a loanword into Greek rather than an inherited item.
items.cn: 希腊语 byrsa 指兽皮或皮袋，一般认为它是借入希腊语的词，而非本土传承。

items.en: Latin bursa named a leather pouch and later a treasury or money chest, which is why the family also touches public money.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 指皮制小袋，后来也指金库、钱柜，所以这个词族也涉及公共资金。

items.en: Medieval Latin kept bursa for a bag and a treasury, while Old French developed borse, the form that carried the word towards England.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留 bursa 指袋子和金库，古法语则发展出 borse，正是把这个词带向英格兰的形式。

items.en: Middle English purs named a small drawstring pouch worn at the belt, carried by men as well as women.
items.cn: 中古英语 purs 指系在腰带上、用细绳收口的小袋，男女都常佩带。

items.en: Everyday modern English narrows the object to a woman's handbag, while the older sense of available money survives in public purse and purse strings.
items.cn: 现代英语日常用法把这个物件收窄为女式手袋，而「可用之钱」的旧义仍活在 public purse 与 purse strings 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same bag word; the near-meaning group collects other words for what holds money or for money itself.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「袋」词上的拼写与同族词；近义组收其他表示装钱的物件或钱本身的词。

entries.definitionCN: 追赶、追求；只是开头几个字母相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The officer on a ship who keeps the accounts and pays the crew.
entries.definitionCN: 船上负责账目与发放薪水的职务。

entries.definition: An official who manages money in a college or school.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学或学校里管理钱财的职务。

entries.definition: To pay money back to someone who has spent it on your behalf.
entries.definitionCN: 把别人替你垫付的钱还给他。

entries.definition: A small flat case for notes and cards, usually carried in a pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 装纸币与卡片的小扁夹，通常放在口袋里。

entries.definition: A bag for personal items, carried especially by women.
entries.definitionCN: 装随身物品的包，尤指女性提包。

entries.definitionCN: 一群人凑起来共用的一笔钱。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to a leather bag, and every later sense still keeps something of that one small container.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词源自一只皮袋，后来每个义项都还留着那只小容器的影子。

normal.en: Bursa in Latin is a leather pouch, and the earliest English purses were exactly that: soft bags closed with string.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 是皮制小袋，英语最早的 purse 正是这种用细绳收口的软袋。

normal.en: Purser keeps the money-handling side of the family: the person on a ship who looks after accounts and pay.
normal.cn: purser 保留了词族中「管钱」的一面：船上负责账目与薪水的人。

normal.en: Reimburse puts re- (back) with a stem from bursa, so the word pictures money going back into the bag it came from.
normal.cn: reimburse 把表示「回」的 re- 与 bursa 的词干结合，画面就是钱回到原来的袋子里。

normal.en: Purse strings were once literal cords; holding them now means controlling the money itself.
normal.cn: purse strings 从前是实实在在的绳子，如今握住它就等于掌控钱财。

normal.en: The public purse treats a whole country's funds as one bag that officials must open with care.
normal.cn: public purse 把一个国家的资金看成一只袋子，官员打开它时必须谨慎。

abstract.en: A purse fits in one hand, yet it can stand for everything a household is able to choose.
abstract.cn: 钱袋一只手就握得住，却可以代表一个家庭所能做的一切选择。

abstract.en: One word names the bag, the money and the prize, because each is something handed from one person to another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指袋子、又指钱和奖金，因为这三样都是从一个人手里交到另一个人手里。

abstract.en: A purse is often closed not by its clasp but by the fear behind it.
abstract.cn: 钱袋往往是靠背后的顾虑合上的，而不是靠那道扣子。

examples.en: She paid the fare from a small purse she kept in her coat.
examples.cn: 她用外套里一只小钱包付了车费。

examples.en: The tour was cancelled because the club's purse was empty.
examples.cn: 巡演取消了，因为俱乐部的资金已经见底。

examples.en: The winner took home a purse of fifty thousand dollars.
examples.cn: 冠军拿走了五万美元奖金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「珀斯」——去澳大利亚的珀斯旅行，得先备好钱包，记住 purse 是钱包、财力。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bag that holds money; the senses divide into the bag itself, the money inside it, and the prize once handed over in such a bag.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是装钱的袋子；义项由此分为袋子本身、袋里的钱，以及从前装在这种袋子里交付的奖金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn leather pouch tucked inside an apron, holding a whole day's earnings.
core.cn: 核心意象：围裙内侧一只磨旧的皮袋，装着一整天的收入。

branches.en: a drawstring pouch on a market stall
branches.cn: 集市摊前一只收口的钱袋

branches.en: a bag whose weight equals a family's choices
branches.cn: 一只袋子的分量等于一个家庭的选择

branches.en: a council counting what it can afford
branches.cn: 市政会算着手里的钱够做什么

branches.en: a prize handed over in a leather bag
branches.cn: 装在皮袋里当场交付的奖金

branches.en: money that is both kept and awarded
branches.cn: 既被存着又被颁出去的同一笔钱

intro.en: The word is held together by a Greek bag word, its Latin descendant, the English noun, and the suffixes that build a person and a paying-back verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的「袋」、它的拉丁后裔、英语名词，以及构成「人」与「偿付」的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 描述；描写；形容
definition_en: to say what something or someone is like in words
core_image: 用文字画出一幅画给别人看
scene: 作文课上老师让我们写公园的春天。 Can you describe the cherry tree in your own words?
sceneCN: 这里 describe 是「描写」（第 1 个义项：用语言呈现样貌）；句意是你能用自己的话描写那棵樱花树吗？

derivatives.zh: 由 describe 变词尾加 -tion 构成，义为「描述；说明书」
由 describe 词根加 -ive 构成，义为「描写的；描述性的」

senses.title: To say what something is like
senses.definition: to give a picture of something in spoken or written words
senses.definitionCN: 用口语或文字呈现事物的样子
senses.example: She described the beach with bright, sunny words.
senses.exampleCN: 她用明亮 sunny 的词句描写那片海滩。
senses.why: Words can paint, so telling what you saw is drawing with the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 文字可以作画，讲述所见就像用舌头画画，这便是描写的本义。

senses.title: To call something a certain way
senses.definition: to say that something has a particular quality
senses.definitionCN: 说某事物具有某种性质
senses.example: Fans described the match as the best of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 球迷们把这场比赛形容为年度最佳。
senses.why: A short label is a fast sketch of the whole thing.
senses.whyCN: 一个简短的形容词是对事物整体的速写，于是有了形容义。

senses.title: To draw a shape in geometry
senses.definition: to draw or trace a shape so that it moves along a line
senses.definitionCN: 沿某条线画出或描出图形
senses.example: The compass describes a perfect circle on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 圆规在黑板上画出标准的圆。
senses.why: Tracing a line is writing in space, the same old root of marking down.
senses.whyCN: 在空间里描线就是一种「写画」，与记下的本义一脉相承。

intro.en: Describe comes from Latin words for writing down.
intro.cn: describe 来自拉丁语中表示「写下、描画」的词。

items.en: Describere meant to copy down or sketch, from de- plus scribere (to write).
items.cn: 拉丁语 describere 意为摹写、描画，由 de- 加 scribere（写）构成。

items.en: Scribere also gave script, scribe and scribble.
items.cn: scribere 还派生了 script、scribe、scribble 等词。

items.en: Old French carried descriivre into learned Latin-based writing.
items.cn: 古法语把 descriivre 带入书面语。

items.en: English took describe in the fifteenth century, first meaning to trace a figure.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 describe，最初意为描出图形。

items.en: The word settled as telling what things are like in words.
items.cn: 现代英语中它定型为用语言呈现事物的样貌。

note.en: These words share the writing root or describe telling about things.
note.cn: 这些词与「书写」词根同源，或同样描述讲述事物。

abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在空中勾勒出一幕场景。

abstract.en: Hear a radio announcer describing the game play by play.
abstract.cn: 听电台解说员一幕一幕描述比赛。

abstract.en: Feel a friend's face light up as your words paint the place.
abstract.cn: 体会你的话语把景色画出来时朋友眼睛发亮的样子。

examples.en: Please describe your best friend so we can guess who it is.
examples.cn: 请描述你最好的朋友，让我们猜猜是谁。

examples.en: The guide described every corner of the old town.
examples.cn: 导游描述了老城的每个角落。

examples.en: It is hard to describe how exciting the sports day was.
examples.cn: 很难形容运动会那天有多激动人心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「低斯克莱」——低头像斯克莱伯一样抄写，把见到的「描述」下来

root: 来自拉丁语 describere（摹写、描画），由 de-（下）加 scribere（写）构成；本义「照着描下来」，引申为「用语言描述」。

sensesIntro.en: Describe writes the world down, then labels it and traces shapes.
sensesIntro.cn: describe 先用文字记录世界，再给它贴标签、描出图形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: drawing a picture with words
core.cn: 核心意象：用文字作画

branches.en: A scene told in words
branches.cn: 用语言讲述的场景

branches.en: A quick quality label
branches.cn: 简短的性质标签

branches.en: A shape traced in space
branches.cn: 空间中描出的图形

branches.en: Portrait and label, two speeds
branches.cn: 画像与标签，两种速度

branches.en: One root: marking down
branches.cn: 同一词根：记画下来

intro.en: Describe is built on the Latin root for writing.
intro.cn: describe 建立在拉丁语「书写」词根上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root scrib or script means to write.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 scrib/script 意为书写。

items.exampleCN: subscribe to a magazine（订阅杂志）

definition_zh: 类型；种类；打字；键入
definition_en: a class of things sharing features, or to write on a keyboard
core_image: 一排金属字模从盒子里被拣出来，按在纸上留下同一形状的印记
scene: 灯光下，一个人把要交的报告一行行敲进电脑。 She typed the last line and saved the file.
sceneCN: 这里 type 是「打字；键入」（第 3 个义项：通过键盘逐个输入字符）；句意为她打完最后一行并保存了文件。指尖在键盘上逐个落下的动作，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 type 加 -ical 构成，义为「典型的」
由 type 加 -ing 构成，义为「打字」
由 type 与 writer 合成，义为「打字机」
由 type 加 -ist 构成，义为「打字员」

senses.title: The family likeness
senses.definition: a group of things that share the same features
senses.definitionCN: 具有相同特征的一类事物
senses.example: This type of engine is common in small boats.
senses.exampleCN: 这种发动机在小船上很常见。
senses.why: The noun first named the shared form, the stamp that made many copies alike.
senses.whyCN: 名词起初指共有的形状，即许多复制品共用的那个印模。

senses.title: The metal letter
senses.definition: a small block of metal with a raised letter used for printing
senses.definitionCN: 印有凸起字母的金属小块，用于印刷
senses.example: The printer sorted the worn type back into its box.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷工把磨旧的活字重新装回字盒。
senses.why: A type was the physical thing that pressed a shape onto paper, the same word for the class and the stamp.
senses.whyCN: 活字正是把形状压到纸上的实物，同一个词兼指类别与印模。

senses.title: The tapping keys
senses.definition: to write by pressing keys on a machine or keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 通过按键在机器或键盘上书写
senses.example: She typed the last line and saved the file.
senses.exampleCN: 她打完最后一行并保存了文件。
senses.why: Since the letters came from type, the act of setting them became typing.
senses.whyCN: 因为字母来自活字，排印它们的动作便成了 typing。

intro.en: Type comes from Greek typos, a blow or the mark a blow leaves, through Latin and French.
intro.cn: type 来自希腊语 typos（一击、一击留下的印），经拉丁语与法语传下。

items.en: Typos meant a blow, and then the mark stamped by a blow.
items.cn: typos 意为击打，进而指击打留下的印痕。

items.en: Typus borrowed the idea of a figure or an image.
items.cn: typus 借来了图案、形象的意思。

items.en: French type narrowed it to a symbol or a model.
items.cn: 法语 type 把它收窄为符号或模型。

items.en: Printing gave it a body: movable type, a block that stamps letters.
items.cn: 印刷使它有了实体：活字，即压出字母的块。

items.en: From printing the word spread to kinds of things and to typing on keys.
items.cn: 从印刷扩展到事物的种类，再扩展到敲键盘。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek stem, the second names classes and keyboard work.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊词干，第二组是类别与键盘操作相关词。

entries.definition: Showing the usual features.
A machine for typing.
A printing mistake.
A class of similar things.
A group in a system of classes.
The set of keys used to type.

normalIntro.en: Type began as a blow and ended as a keyboard: the mark and the making of marks.
normalIntro.cn: type 从一击开始，落到了键盘上：印痕与制造印痕。

normal.en: Type goes with typical, which means showing the type.
normal.cn: type 与 typical 同源，后者意为体现这一类的样子。

normal.en: Type of takes a singular type even before a plural noun.
normal.cn: type of 后用单数 type。

normal.en: Type in means to enter text on a screen.
normal.cn: type in 表示在屏幕上录入。

normal.en: Blood type shows how the word names a class.
normal.cn: blood type 显示它如何命名类别。

normal.en: Typing is not writing by hand, but both leave marks.
normal.cn: 打字不是手写，但都在留下痕迹。

abstract.en: A row of metal letters in a wooden tray.
abstract.cn: 木盘里一排金属字母。

abstract.en: A finger coming down on one key.
abstract.cn: 一根手指落在某个键上。

abstract.en: One shape stamped many times on one page.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状在纸页上被压了许多次。

examples.en: I typed my address into the form.
examples.cn: 我把地址输入了表格。

examples.en: That type of plant needs little water.
examples.cn: 那种植物几乎不需要水。

examples.en: She can type faster than she can write by hand.
examples.cn: 她打字比手写还快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太普」——太普通的一类，大家都属于同一种类型。

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 typus、希腊语 typos（一击、印痕），本义为压出的印记，进而指类别的模型，同族词有 typical、typewriter、typist、typo。

sensesIntro.en: First the class of things, then the metal block that prints them, then the act of pressing keys.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是事物的类别，再是印出字母的金属块，最后是敲键的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal letter pressed on a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在纸上的金属活字。

branches.en: The class branch: many things share one stamp.
branches.cn: 类别分支：许多事物共一个印模。

branches.en: The print branch: the block behind the letter.
branches.cn: 印刷分支：字母背后的那块金属。

branches.en: The key branch: the stamping done by fingers.
branches.cn: 按键分支：用手指完成的压印。

branches.en: The trade branch: printers sort their types.
branches.cn: 行业分支：印刷工整理活字。

branches.en: The machine branch: stamps become keys.
branches.cn: 机器分支：印模变成按键。

intro.en: Type is a Greek root, and the family grows with -ical, -ist, -ing and compounds.
intro.cn: type 是希腊词根，词族靠 -ical、-ist、-ing 及合成扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form typus supplied the whole family, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式 typus 供应了整个词族，列在下面。

definition_zh: 流行音乐；砰的一声；爆开；突然冒出；匆匆去一趟
definition_en: popular music as a genre; a short sharp bursting sound; to burst or open with such a sound; and to appear or go somewhere suddenly
core_image: 手臂边一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，屋里的人全都抬头
scene: 街角的小店门口挂着旧音箱，午后的阳光斜进来，一群学生跟着旋律点头。 The radio kept playing one pop song after another while the students waited for the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 pop 指「流行音乐」（第 1 个义项：旋律好记、面向大众的音乐）；句意为学生们等公交时，收音机一首接一首地放着流行歌。图中可辨识物件：旧音箱、斜照进来的阳光、等车的学生。

pos.zh: 爆开；突然冒出；匆匆去一趟

derivatives.zh: 由 pop 与 corn 复合而成，取「受热爆开」的旧义，义为「爆米花」
由 pop 加表示工具或人的 -er 构成，义为「爆米花锅；按扣」
由 pop 加 -ing 构成，义为「连续的爆响；机械舞」

senses.title: Popular music as a genre
senses.definition: a style of music with a strong beat and easily remembered tunes, made for a wide audience rather than for specialists
senses.definitionCN: 节奏鲜明、旋律好记，面向广大听众而非专业圈子的音乐类型
senses.example: She sang along to every pop song on the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机里每一首流行歌她都跟着唱。
senses.why: This sense is a mid-twentieth-century clipping of popular, taken from phrases such as popular music, so the name says who the music is made for rather than how it is composed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是二十世纪中叶从 popular 截短来的，取的是 popular music 一类说法，所以名字说的是音乐做给谁听，而不是它怎么写。

senses.title: A short sharp bursting sound
senses.definition: a small explosive noise made when something bursts, snaps or is struck
senses.definitionCN: 东西爆开、绷断或被击中时发出的短促爆响
senses.example: The paper bag gave a loud pop when she hit it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一巴掌拍下去，纸袋砰地响了一声。
senses.why: This sense is generally taken to be imitative: the word copies the noise of a small burst, which is why one form can name both the sound and the event behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项一般认为来自拟声：词本身在模仿小东西爆开的声响，所以同一种形式既能指声音，也能指发出声音的那件事。

senses.title: To burst or open with a sharp sound
senses.definition: to burst, open or come out suddenly with a small sharp noise
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着短促响声突然爆开、弹开或冒出来
senses.example: The cork popped out of the bottle and hit the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶塞砰地从瓶口弹出来，撞到了天花板上。
senses.why: Once the sound-word had named the noise of bursting, English could turn it into a verb for whatever produced that noise, and a cork leaving a bottle is the clearest case.
senses.whyCN: 拟声词一旦指认了爆裂的响声，英语就能把它变成动词，指发出这声响的东西；瓶塞飞出瓶口就是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: To appear or go somewhere suddenly
senses.definition: to come into view suddenly and briefly, or to go somewhere quickly for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂地出现在眼前，或很快地去某处一趟
senses.example: A rabbit popped out of the hole and froze.
senses.exampleCN: 一只兔子突然从洞里冒出来，随即定住不动。
senses.why: A burst is sudden and over in a moment; English carries that suddenness over to anything that appears or leaves in a flash, which is how the verb reaches rabbits and short errands.
senses.whyCN: 爆开是一下子发生、一下就结束的；英语把这种突然挪到任何一闪而现或一闪而去的事情上，动词于是能用来说兔子，也能说匆匆跑一趟。

intro.en: English has two words written pop: an imitative syllable for a bang, and a twentieth-century clipping of popular. The spellings merged, the histories did not.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个拼作 pop 的词：一个模仿爆响，一个是二十世纪对 popular 的截短。拼写合流了，来历并没有合流。

items.en: Populus named the people as a body, the crowd whose taste decides what becomes common.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的民众，也就是他们的喜好决定了什么东西会变得普遍。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to or pleasing the people, and it is the adjective that pop would later shorten.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的，正是后来被 pop 截短的那个形容词。

items.en: Generally regarded as imitative, the short word for a small explosion copies the sound itself and has no connection with Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为表示小爆炸的 pop 是拟声词，直接模仿声音，与拉丁语没有关系。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century popular music was clipped to pop, used first as a modifier and soon as a noun in its own right.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶，popular music 被截短成 pop，先作修饰语，很快又独立作名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands: a bang, a quick errand and a whole shelf of music, all spelled the same way.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线都留着：一声爆响、一趟快去快回、一整排音乐，拼写完全一样。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the populus family behind the music sense; the near-meaning group collects other words for popular music and for sudden movement.
note.cn: 形近组顺着音乐义背后的 populus 词族展开；近义组收表示流行音乐与突然动作的其他词。

entries.definition: Liked by many people; the adjective that pop shortens.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的；pop 正是它的截短形式。

entries.definition: The state of being liked or accepted by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱或接受的状况。

entries.definition: To make something widely known or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Corn that bursts open when it is heated.
entries.definitionCN: 受热后爆开的玉米；爆米花。

entries.definition: A loud form of popular music built on guitars and drums.
entries.definitionCN: 以吉他和鼓为主的吵闹流行音乐；摇滚。

entries.definition: A song or record that becomes very successful.
entries.definitionCN: 非常成功的歌曲或唱片；热门歌曲。

entries.definition: The music, taste or opinion accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被大多数人接受的音乐、品味或观点；主流。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two histories at once: a copied sound and a shortened adjective, and most of its uses can be traced to one or the other.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时背着两段来历：一个模仿来的声音，一个被截短的形容词；它的用法大多能归到其中一条。

normal.en: Popular music was shortened to pop, so a pop song is simply a song meant for everybody.
normal.cn: popular music 被缩成 pop，所以 pop song 就是给所有人听的歌。

normal.en: The bang is imitative: say the word sharply and you have already made the sound.
normal.cn: 爆响那个义项是拟声的：把这个词短促地念出来，声音就已经发出来了。

normal.en: Pop up keeps the idea of a burst: something appears as if it had just exploded into view.
normal.cn: pop up 保留了「突然爆开」的意思：某物像是刚炸出来一样出现在眼前。

normal.en: Pop into a shop applies the same suddenness to a short errand, in and out in a moment.
normal.cn: pop into a shop 把同一种突然用在短程跑腿上，进去又出来，只用一会儿。

normal.en: Popcorn is named for the moment the kernel bursts, so the compound preserves the oldest sense.
normal.cn: popcorn 得名于玉米粒爆开的那一刻，这个复合词保存了最古老的义项。

abstract.en: One syllable carries both a drum hit and a hit song: noise and culture share a spelling.
abstract.cn: 一个音节既装着鼓点的一击，也装着一首热门歌：声音和文化共用一种拼写。

abstract.en: A balloon, a cork, a rabbit: the same snap marks every sudden appearance.
abstract.cn: 气球、瓶塞、兔子：同一声脆响标记着每一次突然出现。

abstract.en: Pop is what a crowd makes common, so the word for the people sits silently inside it.
abstract.cn: pop 指人群使之变得普遍的东西，所以表示民众的那个词静静藏在它里面。

examples.en: The children danced to a pop song in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 孩子们在厨房里跟着一首流行歌跳舞。

examples.en: The balloon popped and the dog ran off.
examples.cn: 气球砰地爆了，狗跑开了。

examples.en: A message popped up on the screen.
examples.cn: 屏幕上突然弹出一条消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡泡」——泡泡一破就是砰的一声；pop 又是人人会哼的流行歌。

root: 一般认为有两个来源：表示爆响的 pop 是拟声词；表示流行音乐的 pop 是 popular 的截短形式，而 popular 出自拉丁语 populus（民众）。

sensesIntro.en: Two origins feed one spelling: the sharp sound and its suddenness on one side, mass-market music on the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种来历汇成一个拼写：一边是爆响与随之而来的突然，另一边是面向大众的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon bursting at arm's length, its skin flying off while everyone looks up.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂边上一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，所有人都抬头看。

branches.en: a phone playing a three-minute song at full volume
branches.cn: 手机以最大音量放一首三分钟的歌

branches.en: a paper bag bursting under a slap
branches.cn: 一巴掌拍破的纸袋

branches.en: a cork flying across the kitchen
branches.cn: 瓶塞飞过厨房

branches.en: someone dashing into a shop for milk
branches.cn: 有人冲进小店买牛奶

branches.en: one short word for a bang and for a hit tune
branches.cn: 一个短词同时指爆响和热门曲子

intro.en: The word rests on two layers: an imitative English syllable, and the Latin family of populus. In that family -ar builds the adjective popular, -ity builds the noun of state, and -ize builds the verb of making; pop itself is only a clipping of the -ar form.
intro.cn: 这个词压着两层东西：一个拟声的英语音节，以及拉丁语 populus 词族。在这个词族里，-ar 造形容词 popular，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词；pop 本身只是那个 -ar 形容词的截短。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: of or belonging to the people
burst with a short sharp sound
relating to, of the kind of
corn that bursts open when heated
items.meaningCN: 复合词：受热爆开的玉米

items.meaning: a repeated bursting sound or a dance style
items.meaningCN: 名词：连续的爆响；机械舞

definition_zh: 贸易；交易；行业；手艺；（作动词）交易；从事贸易
definition_en: the activity of buying and selling goods, or a kind of work that needs skill, and to buy and sell or exchange
core_image: 集市上两只手把货物和钱交换过来
scene: 码头边的集市一早开市，盐、布和铁器在不同的摊位上被换来换去。 The two ports have traded salt and timber for three hundred years.
sceneCN: 这里 trade 是「贸易」（第 1 个义项：买进卖出的商业活动）；句意为这两个港口三百年来一直进行盐与木材的贸易。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「商人；交易者」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「交易；买卖」
由 trade 加 mark 合成，义为「商标」

senses.title: The buying and selling of goods
senses.definition: the business of exchanging goods or services between people, companies, or countries
senses.definitionCN: 个人、公司或国家之间交换货物或服务的活动
senses.example: Trade between the two islands stopped during the storm season.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴季期间两座岛之间的贸易中断了。
senses.why: The word first named a track or a beaten path, and trade was the traffic that moved along those paths.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一条被踩出来的路线，而贸易正是沿着这些路线流动的往来。

senses.title: A skilled occupation
senses.definition: a kind of work, usually one needing training with the hands, such as carpentry
senses.definitionCN: 一种通常需要手上训练的工作，如木工
senses.example: His trade was that of a wheelwright.
senses.exampleCN: 他的本行是造车轮。
senses.why: Crafts were once practised along particular streets, so the way of making a living took the name of the path.
senses.whyCN: 手艺活儿曾集中在特定街道上经营，于是谋生的方式也沿用了「路」这个名称。

senses.title: A particular branch of business
senses.definition: all the businesses that deal in one kind of goods or service, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 经营同一类商品或服务的所有商家的总称
senses.example: The book trade fears the new tax on paper.
senses.exampleCN: 图书业界担心新的纸张税。
senses.why: When many people share one occupation, the occupation itself becomes a collective body with its own interests.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人从事同一行，这门职业本身就成了有自身利益的集体。

senses.title: To exchange one thing for another
senses.definition: to give something to someone and receive something else in return
senses.definitionCN: 把某物给某人，同时换回另一样东西
senses.example: The boys traded marbles for a football card.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们用弹珠换了一张足球卡。
senses.why: Any buying and selling is at bottom an exchange, so the noun turns into a simple verb of swapping.
senses.whyCN: 买卖归根到底就是交换，于是名词变成简单的「互换」动词。

senses.title: To deal in goods professionally
senses.definition: to run a business that buys and sells a stated kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 经营买卖某类特定商品的生意
senses.example: The firm trades in coffee and cocoa.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司经营咖啡与可可。
senses.why: The verb with in marks the goods that the business lives by, as opposed to goods swapped in passing.
senses.whyCN: 动词后加 in 标记这家生意赖以生存的商品，与随手换东西不同。

senses.title: Swapping one problem for another
senses.definition: in phrases like trade places, to exchange positions or situations with someone
senses.definitionCN: 如 trade places 一类说法中，与某人交换位置或处境
senses.example: For a day the two managers traded places to see the work from below.
senses.exampleCN: 两位经理交换了一天位置，从下面看看这份工作。
senses.why: Once the verb means swap, it can swap anything, including roles that are not goods at all.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个动词表示互换，它就可以换任何东西，包括根本不是商品的角色。

intro.en: Trade comes from Middle Low German trade, a track or course, and the sense of commerce grew in English from traffic moving along such paths.
intro.cn: trade 来自中古低地德语 trade（路线、轨道），「商业」这一含义是在英语中由沿这些路线往来的货运生长出来的。

items.en: Middle Low German trade means a track, a course, or a beaten way.
items.cn: 中古低地德语 trade 意为路径、走向或踩出来的道。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century with the sense of a regular course or way of life.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，意为惯常的路线或生活方式。

items.en: From the course of travelling merchants come the senses of traffic, commerce, and finally buying and selling between nations.
items.cn: 从商人往来的路线，发展出货运、商业，最后是国与国之间的买卖。

items.en: In the sixteenth century trade also settles into the sense of a skilled craft or occupation.
items.cn: 十六世纪，trade 又固定为指一门需要技艺的行当或职业。

items.en: The verb and phrases such as trade union spread in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries with industrial growth.
items.cn: 动词用法以及 trade union 一类说法随着工业成长在十八、十九世纪流行开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same trade stem, and the near-meaning group gathers commercial terms.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在同一 trade 词干上的词，近义组收集商业术语。

entries.definition: a person who buys and sells
the activity of buying and selling
a registered sign of a business
to walk or step
entries.definitionCN: 踩；踏，拼写相近而来源不同

entries.definition: large-scale trade between businesses
the work of making and selling things
a job that needs training and skill

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the original sense of a path, from the compounds, and from the verb patterns with in and for.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「路径」这一原义、复合词以及动词后接 in、for 的模式入手。

normal.en: Trade began as a track, so trade is the traffic on that track.
normal.cn: trade 原是「路线」，所以贸易就是这条路线上的人流物流。

normal.en: Trade in coffee means dealing in coffee; trade with a country means doing business with it.
normal.cn: trade in coffee 是经营咖啡，trade with a country 是与某国做生意。

normal.en: Trade union, trade fair, trade mark: in front of a noun the word means belonging to business.
normal.cn: trade union、trade fair、trade mark，放在名词前就表示「属于商业的」。

normal.en: By trade means by occupation, showing the old craft sense.
normal.cn: by trade 意为「就职业而言」，显示古老的「手艺」义项。

normal.en: Trader and trading split the verb into a person and an activity.
normal.cn: trader 与 trading 把这个动词分成人和活动两面。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting over a table, one holding a sack, the other coins.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在桌上相握，一只握着袋子，一只握着硬币。

abstract.en: Think of a road that gets deeper as more carts use it, and the carts are the trade.
abstract.cn: 想一条路越被车轧越深，而那些车就是贸易。

abstract.en: Trade is trust that has been made repeatable.
abstract.cn: 贸易是被做成可重复的信任。

examples.en: The town grew rich on the wool trade.
examples.cn: 这个镇靠羊毛贸易富了起来。

examples.en: By trade he was a carpenter, but he spent his nights writing.
examples.cn: 他本行是木匠，却把夜晚都用来写作。

examples.en: The two children traded hats and laughed.
examples.cn: 两个孩子换着帽子，笑了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹得」——生意吹得再大，也是一手交钱一手交货。

root: 中古低地德语 trade（路线、轨道）→ 中古英语 trade（常走的路、生活方式）→ 现代英语 trade（贸易；行业）。词族有 trader、trading、trademark。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from a path, turns it into the commerce that travels it, then into the skilled calling practised on it, then into the whole industry, and ends with the verb of swapping anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从小路出发，转成沿着它流动的商业，再成为路上经营的行当与整个业界，最后落在一换一切东西的动词上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods and money passing between two hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：货物与钱在两只手之间交换。

branches.en: The commerce that moves along the routes.
branches.cn: 沿着路线流动的商业。

branches.en: The skilled work of a person.
branches.cn: 一个人熟练的谋生手艺。

branches.en: The whole body of that business.
branches.cn: 整个业界的整体。

branches.en: The plain act of swapping, including roles.
branches.cn: 纯粹互换的动作，包括角色。

branches.en: The professional dealing in stated goods.
branches.cn: 以特定商品为业。

intro.en: The word is a Low German borrowing with no productive suffix, and its family is built with -er, -ing, and compounds such as mark.
intro.cn: 本词是低地德语借词，没有能产后缀，其词族由 -er、-ing 以及 mark 一类复合成分构成。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin source, so no Latin entries are listed; the nearest Latin vocabulary is commercial rather than etymological.
latinIntro.cn: 本词没有拉丁语来源，因此不列拉丁词条；拉丁语中最近的词汇只是意义上的商务用语，并非同源。

Trading runs all day on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 交易大厅里全天都在交易。

items.exampleCN: trades 既是复数也是动词形式。

items.example: A trade union protects skilled workers.
A trade fair shows new goods.
items.exampleCN: 贸易博览会展示新商品。

items.example: Free trade means open buying and selling.
items.exampleCN: 自由贸易就是开放的买卖。

definition_zh: 便宜地；廉价地；花费少地
definition_en: in a way that costs little money; at a low price
core_image: 用几张零钱就把东西拎回家
scene: 文具店打折，我三块钱买到了两支钢笔。 I managed to buy two pens quite cheaply at the sale.
sceneCN: 这里 cheaply 是「便宜地」（第 1 个义项：花钱少）；句意是我在促销时便宜地买了两支钢笔。

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础，义为「便宜的」
由 cheap 加 -ness 构成，义为「便宜；廉价」
cheap 的比较级，义为「更便宜的」

senses.title: At a low price
senses.definition: in a way that costs only a little money
senses.definitionCN: 花钱很少的方式
senses.example: Students can eat cheaply at the school canteen.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在学校食堂吃饭很省钱。
senses.why: The word takes cheap and turns the low price into a manner.
senses.whyCN: 它把 cheap 的低价变成一种方式。

senses.title: With little effort or cost of quality
senses.definition: made with poor materials in order to save money
senses.definitionCN: 为省钱而用料低劣地制作
senses.example: The toy was cheaply made and broke in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这玩具做工廉价，一天就坏了。
senses.why: Low price sometimes walks hand in hand with low quality.
senses.whyCN: 低价有时与低质相伴。

senses.title: Without wasting money
senses.definition: carefully, so money is not wasted
senses.definitionCN: 精打细算、不浪费钱地
senses.example: Our family travels cheaply by taking night trains.
senses.exampleCN: 我们家坐夜车旅行，节省开支。
senses.why: Spending little can also mean spending wisely.
senses.whyCN: 花得少也可以是花得聪明。

intro.en: Cheap comes from an old word for trade, not for price.
intro.cn: cheap 源自表示「交易」的古词，而非「价格」。

items.en: Old English ceap meant trade, buying and selling.
items.cn: 古英语 ceap 意为交易、买卖。

items.en: Chipping, now a London street name, once meant a market.
items.cn: Chipping（伦敦街名）曾意为市场。

items.en: At the market, goods that sold at good bargains came to be called cheap.
items.cn: 市场上讨价好成交的货物渐渐被称为 cheap。

items.en: The sense narrowed from the trade itself to the low price.
items.cn: 词义从「交易」收窄为「低价」。

items.en: The adverb cheaply formed with the common -ly ending.
items.cn: 副词 cheaply 按常见规则加 -ly 构成。

note.en: One family about low prices and smart spending.
note.cn: 围绕低价与精打细算的词族。

normalIntro.en: Start from cheap, then add the adverb tail.
normalIntro.cn: 从 cheap 出发，再加副词尾巴。

normal.en: cheap means costing little.
normal.cn: cheap 意为便宜。

normal.en: cheaply = cheap + -ly, in a cheap way.
normal.cn: cheaply 由 cheap 加 -ly 构成，便宜地。

normal.en: buy cheaply, spend less.

normal.en: cheaply made can mean badly made.
normal.cn: cheaply made 有时指做工差。

abstract.en: Picture two heavy bags: one costs ten coins, one costs two.
abstract.cn: 想象两个大袋子：一个花十枚硬币，一个只花两枚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin pig that smiles when you save at the market.
abstract.cn: 想象市场省钱时存钱罐露出笑容。

abstract.en: Picture a cheap toy snapping apart the first time you play.
abstract.cn: 想象廉价玩具一玩就散架。

examples.en: We can eat cheaply at the noodle shop near school.
examples.cn: 在学校附近的面馆吃饭很便宜。

examples.en: Second-hand books let us study cheaply.
examples.cn: 二手书让我们低成本地学习。

examples.en: The bag looked good but was cheaply sewn.
examples.cn: 这包看着不错，但缝制得很廉价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欺普利」——用很少的钱欺负了普通价格，捡了大便宜，所以「欺普利」= cheaply。

root: 古英语 ceap（交易）→ 中古英语 cheap（低价买到）→ cheap + -ly。与 chapman（小贩）、Chipping 街名同源。

sensesIntro.cn: 低价、廉价或节俭。

branches.cn: 用料低劣地制造

The cheapest seat is still good.

definition_zh: 工具；器具；手段；（软件）工具；用工具加工
definition_en: an object, usually held in the hand, that is made to help do work, or any means used to achieve something
core_image: 一只木柄的手锤靠在墙边，锤头上的磨痕说明它被用得很多
scene: 木工台面上散着凿子、卷尺和几块未刨的木料，墙上的木板插满了带柄的工具。 He laid each tool back in its place before turning off the light.
sceneCN: 这里 tool 是「工具」这一类物件（第 1 个义项：手持以帮助工作的器物）；句意为他在关灯前把每件工具都放回原位。画面里有木工台、凿子、卷尺与墙上挂满工具的木架。

pos.zh: 动词：用工具加工；给……装上工具

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「工具（复数）」
由 tool 与 kit 合成，义为「工具套装；方法组合」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「模具工装；加工」
由 tool 与 box 合成，义为「工具箱」

senses.title: An object made to help with work
senses.definition: a device, usually held in the hand, that is made to do a job more easily
senses.definitionCN: 通常手持的器具，制成以后使工作更容易完成
senses.example: A good spade is the only tool you need for this bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这块花圃只需要一把好铲子这件工具。
senses.why: The word is one of the oldest in English, and the earliest senses cover any instrument of labour.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语最古老的词之一，最早的义项涵盖任何劳作器械。

senses.title: A means of achieving something
senses.definition: anything used by a person or group to reach an end
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体用来达到目的的任何东西
senses.example: Language is the chief tool of the historian.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是历史学家的主要工具。
senses.why: Anything that extends what a person can do counts as an instrument, so the word moves easily from metal to method.
senses.whyCN: 任何能扩展人所能做之事的东西都算器械，所以这个词很自然地从金属移到方法。

senses.title: A person used by another
senses.definition: someone who is used by others to do their work or to carry out their plans
senses.definitionCN: 被他人利用来做事或实现其计划的人
senses.example: He was a tool of the men who really ran the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他不过是真正操控委员会那些人手里的工具。
senses.why: A person who merely carries out another's purpose is treated like an implement, and the metaphor is deliberately unkind.
senses.whyCN: 只是实现他人目的的人被当成器物，这个比喻是刻意刻薄的。

senses.title: A set of software functions
senses.definition: a program or function that helps carry out a specific task
senses.definitionCN: 帮助完成某项特定任务的程序或功能
senses.example: The new tool lets you compare two versions of the same document.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新工具可以比较同一文档的两个版本。
senses.why: Software repeats the oldest pattern in the language: a thing made to make work easier, this time without metal.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复了语言里最古老的一套用法：为使工作更易而造出的东西，只是这回没有金属。

senses.title: The cutting part of a machine
senses.definition: the cutting or shaping part of a machine, such as a drill bit
senses.definitionCN: 机床中切削或成形的部件，如钻头
senses.example: Change the tool before the edge dulls completely.
senses.exampleCN: 在刃口完全变钝之前换掉刀具。
senses.why: A machine works by cutting with a tool, so the cutting part inherits the name of the hand tool it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 机器靠刀具切削工作，于是这个切削部件继承了他所取代的手持工具之名。

senses.title: To shape with tools
senses.definition: to cut, shape, or decorate something with a tool
senses.definitionCN: 用工具切割、成形或装饰某物
senses.example: The leather was tooled with a small floral pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这块皮革用小花纹压出了图案。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: to work a material with a tool until a pattern appears.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：用工具加工材料，直到出现花纹。

senses.title: To equip for work
senses.definition: to provide a workshop or factory with the tools it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为作坊或工厂提供所需的工具
senses.example: The plant was tooled up for a new model in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在春季为一种新车型配齐了工装。
senses.why: Equipping a plant is giving it tools at industrial scale, and the same verb covers the workshop and the shop floor.
senses.whyCN: 给工厂装备工具就是工业规模上的「给工具」，同一个动词兼指车间与流水线。

senses.title: To drive a vehicle
senses.definition: in informal speech, to drive a vehicle, especially steadily along
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指开车，尤指平稳前行
senses.example: We tooled along the river road all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个下午沿着河边公路开车闲逛。
senses.why: The slang sense treats a car as the tool of the journey and the driving as working it along.
senses.whyCN: 俚语义把汽车当作旅程的工具，开车就是把这件工具一路使过去。

senses.title: A plain phrase in computing
senses.definition: a small program run from a command line to perform one task quickly
senses.definitionCN: 在命令行运行以快速完成单项任务的小程序
senses.example: A single command-line tool replaced three old scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 一个命令行工具就取代了三个旧脚本。
senses.why: Computing names its small single-purpose programs tools because each one does one job well in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域把单项用途的小程序称作工具，因为每一件就在手中把一件事做好。

intro.en: Tool is an inherited Germanic word, recorded in Old English as tol, and its prehistory beyond the Germanic languages is uncertain.
intro.cn: tool 是继承的日耳曼语词，古英语记作 tol，其在日耳曼语系之外的更早来源尚不确定。

items.en: Tol is used of any instrument or implement, including weapons and writing implements.
items.cn: 古英语 tol 用于任何器械或工具，包括武器与书写用具。

items.en: The stem tolam is shared with Old Norse tol and related forms meaning an implement.
items.cn: 词干 tolam 与古诺斯语 tol 以及表示工具的若干同源形式共有。

items.en: Middle English tool spreads to cover hand tools of every trade and keeps the general sense of a means.
items.cn: 中古英语 tool 扩展到各种手艺的手持工具，并保留「手段」的一般含义。

items.en: The verb appears in the nineteenth century, first for shaping by hand and later for fitting a factory with machines.
items.cn: 动词用法出现于十九世纪，先指手工成形，后指为工厂配备机器。

items.en: The slang sense of a person used by others is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 「被人利用的人」这一俚语义自十六世纪有记录。

items.en: Computing borrows the word for programs, and software tools become one of the commonest uses today.
items.cn: 计算机领域借用这个词指程序，软件工具成了今天最常见的用法之一。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and near spellings, while the near-meaning group gathers words for instruments and for means.
note.cn: 形近组收集复合词与近似拼写，近义组则汇集表示器具与手段的词。

a box for keeping tools
the tools and equipment needed for manufacture
also, or excessively

a simple tool used out of doors or in a trade
a machine made for a particular purpose

normalIntro.en: These memories use the Old English word, the compounds with box and kit, and the way the word slides from objects to means to software.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用古英语原词、与 box 和 kit 构成的复合词，以及这个词由实物滑向手段再到软件的过程。

normal.en: Old English tol is short and plain, and it still names anything that helps you work.
normal.cn: 古英语 tol 简短朴素，至今仍指任何帮着干活的东西。

normal.en: Toolbox and toolkit add box and kit, and both mean a container plus what is in it.
normal.cn: toolbox 与 toolkit 分别加 box 与 kit，都表示容器及其中的东西。

normal.en: A tool for doing something is the abstract sense, and for signals it.
normal.cn: a tool for doing something 是抽象义，介词 for 明确标示。

normal.en: Power tools are driven by motors, and the modifier tells you the power source.
normal.cn: power tools 由电机驱动，修饰语说明动力来源。

normal.en: Software tools borrow the plain word because a good program feels like a well-kept hammer.
normal.cn: 软件工具借用这个朴素的词，因为一个好程序像一把保养良好的锤子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching without looking for the hammer that is always in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不看就伸向那柄永远放在原处的锤子。

abstract.en: Think of a simple blade that turns a difficult job into an easy one.
abstract.cn: 想一件简单的刃具，把难活变成易活。

abstract.en: A tool is a hand made harder, longer, or sharper by design.
abstract.cn: 工具是被设计得更硬、更长或更锐利的手。

examples.en: Please put the tools back in the box when you finish.
examples.cn: 做完以后请把工具放回箱子里。

examples.en: Statistics are a tool, not an answer in themselves.
examples.cn: 统计是一种工具，本身不是答案。

examples.en: The workshop was tooled for bicycle frames only.
examples.cn: 那家车间只配备了生产自行车车架的工装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「图」——做工程先看图纸，再动手拿工具。

root: 古英语 tol（器具、工具），日耳曼语同源词干 tolam；更早来源不确定。含义由实物器具扩展到抽象手段，二十世纪又扩展到软件工具。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the object in the hand, then reaches for means, for people used by others, for the cutting edge of a machine, and finally for the programs and the verb senses that grew from the same plain word.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从手中的器物写起，继而伸向手段、被利用的人、机床的刃口，最后是同一个朴素词形长出的软件与动词义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn handle in the hand that makes work possible.
core.cn: 核心意象：手中被磨旧的握柄，使工作得以完成。

branches.en: The object in the hand and the cutting part of a machine.
branches.cn: 手中之物与机床的刃口。

branches.en: Means, software functions, and command-line programs.
branches.cn: 手段、软件功能与命令行程序。

branches.en: A person treated as an instrument.
branches.cn: 被当作器械的人。

branches.en: The verb of shaping and of equipping.
branches.cn: 表示成形与配备的动词用法。

branches.en: The slang verb for driving.
branches.cn: 表示开车的口语动词。

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic stem with almost no affixes; its growth is by compounding with box, kit, and bar.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的日耳曼语词干，几乎不带词缀，其扩展主要靠与 box、kit、bar 等合成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for the word itself; the Latin entries below belong to borrowed relatives such as instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 本词本身没有拉丁语来源；下列拉丁词条属于 instrument 一类借入的亲属词。

items.example: The stem is unchanged in spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干拼写没有变化。

items.example: The Old English form has one l.
items.exampleCN: 古英语形式只有一个 l。
tooled leather 指压花成形的皮革。

items.example: Tooling can mean the tools of a plant.

items.meaning: a set of things for one purpose

items.example: Toolbar names the strip of buttons on a screen.
items.exampleCN: toolbar 指屏幕上的按钮条。

items.example: Power tools replaced many hand tools.
items.exampleCN: 电动工具取代了许多手工工具。

latinEntries.meaning: a tool, an implement, an instrument

definition_zh: 诊所；门诊部；（短期的）讲习班
definition_en: a place where people receive medical treatment but do not stay overnight
core_image: 一张安静的诊疗床，医生坐在床边问诊
scene: 放学后，妈妈带弟弟去小区的门诊部看嗓子。 The doctor at the clinic checked his throat quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 clinic 是「诊所；门诊部」（第 1 个义项：可以看病但不用住院的地方）；句意是诊所医生很快检查了他的喉咙。

derivatives.zh: 由 clinic  + suffix  -al 构成，义为「临床的；诊所的」
由 clinic  + suffix  -ician 构成，义为「临床医生」

senses.title: A place for medical treatment without staying overnight
senses.definition: a place where a doctor treats patients who do not stay there
senses.definitionCN: 医生为无需留宿的病人看病的地方
senses.example: The new clinic near the station opens at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 车站附近的新诊所八点开门。
senses.why: Doctors once taught at the bedside of patients, and the place where this happened became the clinic.
senses.whyCN: 医生早先在病人床边教学查房，这一地点便得名 clinic。

senses.title: A special medical service or course
senses.titleCN: 专科门诊；（学校的）健康服务
senses.definition: an organized medical service for one special problem
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一专门问题的医疗服务
senses.example: The school runs an eye clinic every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 学校每年春天开设眼科门诊。
senses.why: One problem, one room, one team: medicine splits big care into focused little units.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题、一间诊室、一组医生：医疗把大病区拆成聚焦的小单元。

senses.title: A short course of practical teaching
senses.definition: a short class where a skill is taught in practice
senses.definitionCN: 短期传授某项技能的实践课
senses.example: Uncle Wang teaches at a free basketball clinic on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 王叔叔周日在免费篮球训练营教球。
senses.why: Doctors' bedside lessons felt like coaching, so other sports borrowed the word for skill classes.
senses.whyCN: 医生的床边教学像示范训练，其他项目便借用这个词指技能班。

intro.en: Clinic begins with a bed: the whole word family grows from lying down.
intro.cn: clinic 始于一张床：整个词族都从「躺卧」生长出来。

items.en: Greek kline meant a bed or couch on which sick people lay.
items.cn: 希腊语 kline 指病人躺卧的床或长榻。

items.en: Latin clinicus described a doctor who visited patients at their beds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clinicus 描述到病床边诊视的医生。

items.en: French clinique kept the bedside sense for medical teaching hospitals.
items.cn: 法语 clinique 保留了「床边教学医院」的含义。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century for bedside medical teaching.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该词，指床边医学教学。

items.en: Later English used clinic for the building and then for short practical courses.
items.cn: 后来 clinic 又指诊所建筑，再引申为短期讲习班。

note.en: The first group collects the clinic word family; the second collects places that give care.
note.cn: 第一组收 clinic 词族，第二组收提供医疗照护的场所。

entries.definition: Relating to the treatment of patients.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「临床的」，由 clinic 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A doctor who works directly with patients.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「临床医生」，由 clinic 加 -ician 构成。

entries.definition: To hold on tightly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「紧抓」，拼写与 clinic 开头相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: A large place for serious illness and overnight care.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「医院」，规模更大、可住院。

entries.definition: In British English, a doctor's office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语义为「医生的诊室」。

entries.definition: A small room for sick students or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「医务室」，常在学校或工厂。

normalIntro.en: Remember clinic through its bed root and its family words.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「床」的词根与词族记忆 clinic。

normal.en: clinic comes from a Greek word for bed.
normal.cn: clinic 来自希腊语「床」。

normal.en: clinical means connected with treating patients.
normal.cn: clinical 意为「临床的」。

normal.en: clinician is the doctor in a clinic.
normal.cn: clinician 指诊所里的临床医生。

normal.en: A dental clinic cares for teeth.
normal.cn: dental clinic 看牙。

normal.en: Sports teams hold clinics to teach skills.
normal.cn: 运动队用 clinic 开设技能班。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor pulling a chair beside a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象医生把椅子拉到床边坐下。

abstract.en: Hear the low murmur of questions and answers at the bedside.
abstract.cn: 听床边一问一答的低语。

abstract.en: Feel the calm order of a small, tidy consulting room.
abstract.cn: 感受小诊室里安静有序的气氛。

examples.en: Grandma goes to the clinic for her blood test every month.
examples.cn: 奶奶每个月去诊所验血。

examples.en: The sports clinic taught me how to pass the ball.
examples.cn: 训练营教会了我怎么传球。

examples.en: The clinic was quiet because the doctor was out on a call.
examples.cn: 诊所很安静，因为医生出诊去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克里尼克」——病人躺在「床」上，医生克勤克俭地护理，clinic 就是床边的小诊所。

root: 希腊语 kline（床）→ 拉丁语 clinicus（到床边诊视的医生）→ 法语 clinique → 十八世纪英语 clinic（床边教学）→ 现代英语「诊所」；派生词有 clinical（临床的）、clinician（临床医生）。

sensesIntro.en: Clinic grew from a bedside lesson to a treatment room and a training class.
sensesIntro.cn: clinic 从床边教学延伸到诊疗室，再到技能训练班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the doctor's chair beside the patient's bed
core.cn: 核心意象：病床边医生的那把椅子

branches.en: The treatment room
branches.cn: 看病的场所

branches.en: One problem, one service
branches.cn: 针对单一问题的门诊

branches.en: A short skill class
branches.cn: 短期技能班

branches.en: Everyday medical care
branches.cn: 日常医疗照护

branches.en: Learning by practice
branches.cn: 在实践中学习

intro.en: The bed root builds a whole medical family.
intro.cn: 「床」词根繁衍出整个医疗词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin and Greek roots kline and clinare both come from the same idea of leaning and lying.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kline 与拉丁语 clinare 都出自「倚靠、躺卧」这同一个意象。

items.example: She watched the clinical practice video.
Greek kline lies inside the word clinic.
items.exampleCN: clinic 一词里藏着希腊语 kline。
