items.example: I incline towards the second plan.

items.structure: Latin root clin  with prefix de-
items.example: Sales began to decline in May.

items.structure: Latin root clin  with prefix re-
items.example: The seat reclines for a rest.
The polyclinic sees both eyes and teeth.
items.exampleCN: 综合门诊部既看眼也看牙。

latinEntries.meaning: a doctor who treats patients at the bedside
to visit and examine the sick

definition_zh: 蜜蜂；蜂类昆虫；拼字比赛；忙碌的人
definition_en: a flying insect that collects nectar and makes honey, also used in a few fixed phrases
core_image: 一只在花丛间采蜜的蜂，后腿上挂着两团黄花粉
scene: 花园里，一只蜜蜂围着向日葵转了两圈，然后飞回蜂巢。 A bee landed on the yellow flower and began to collect pollen.
sceneCN: 这里 bee 是「蜜蜂」（第 1 个义项：采蜜的蜂类昆虫）；句意为一只蜜蜂落在黄花上，开始采集花粉。

pos.zh: 名词：蜜蜂；蜂类；拼字比赛

derivatives.zh: 由 bee 与 hive 组合而成，义为「蜂箱；蜂巢」
由 bee 与 keeper 组合而成，义为「养蜂人」
由 bee 与 wax 组合而成，义为「蜂蜡」

senses.title: The honey-making insect
senses.definition: a flying insect with four wings that collects nectar from flowers and makes honey
senses.definitionCN: 一种有四片翅膀、从花中采蜜并酿蜜的飞虫
senses.example: A bee landed on the yellow flower.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜜蜂落在黄花上。
senses.why: Old English beo named this insect, and every Germanic sister language points at the same buzzing creature, so the insect is the oldest and strongest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beo 就指这种昆虫，日耳曼语各亲属语言都指同一只会嗡嗡叫的虫子，所以「蜜蜂」是最古老也最稳固的义项。

senses.title: Bees as a group
senses.definition: any of a large group of related stinging insects, whether or not they make honey
senses.definitionCN: 一大类有近缘关系、会蜇人的昆虫，无论是否酿蜜
senses.example: Bees and wasps look alike to many people.
senses.exampleCN: 在很多人眼里，蜜蜂和黄蜂长得差不多。
senses.why: Because the common bee and its relatives share a body plan and a sting, the name spread from the honey bee to the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 因为常见的蜜蜂与近亲共享同一体型和一根蜇针，这个名字就从蜜蜂扩展到了整类昆虫。

senses.title: A spelling bee
senses.definition: a contest in which people, especially children, spell words aloud and are eliminated when they miss
senses.definitionCN: 一种比赛，参加者尤其多为儿童，轮流口头拼写单词，拼错即被淘汰
senses.example: She won the school spelling bee.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校的拼字比赛中获胜。
senses.why: An old bee meant a gathering of neighbours to work together, and spelling bee kept the gathering sense while narrowing it to a contest in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的 bee 指邻里聚在一起互相帮工，spelling bee 保留了「聚会」的意思，只把内容收窄成拼写竞赛。

senses.title: A busy person
senses.definition: used in the phrase a busy bee for someone who is always active and working
senses.definitionCN: 用在 a busy bee 这一说法中，指总是忙忙碌碌做事的人
senses.example: My aunt is a busy bee in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我姨妈在厨房里忙个不停。
senses.why: A bee never stops moving from flower to flower, so the insect became a natural picture for a person who cannot sit still.
senses.whyCN: 蜜蜂从一朵花飞到另一朵花，从不停歇，于是这只昆虫自然成了形容坐不住的人的画面。

intro.en: Bee is an old Germanic insect name; the gathering sense is a later English development.
intro.cn: bee 是古老的日耳曼语昆虫名；「聚会」义是后来在英语里发展出来的。

items.en: Old English beo named the honey-making insect, and the word was already short and common.
items.cn: 古英语 beo 指酿蜜的昆虫，这个词当时已很短、很常用。

items.en: Dutch bij and German Biene are close relatives, and all go back to one Germanic name for the insect.
items.cn: 荷兰语 bij 与德语 Biene 是近亲，都可追溯到同一个日耳曼语昆虫名。

items.en: The spelling settled as bee, while the meaning stayed firmly on the insect.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 bee，词义则稳定留在这种昆虫上。

items.en: In early modern English a bee could also mean a gathering of neighbours working together, as in a husking bee.
items.cn: 在近代早期英语里，bee 还可以指邻里聚在一起干活，例如剥玉米的聚会 husking bee。

items.en: That gathering sense now survives mainly in spelling bee, while the insect remains the everyday meaning.
items.cn: 那个「聚会」义如今主要保留在 spelling bee 里，而昆虫义仍是日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words built on the same sounds; the near-meaning group collects other stinging insects.
note.cn: 形近组收同一批读音很短的词；近义组收其他会蜇人的昆虫。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to exist or to have a quality; it sounds exactly like bee.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「是、存在」，读音与 bee 完全相同。

entries.definition: The meat of cattle; it begins with the same long vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「牛肉」，以同一个长元音开头。

entries.definition: A kind of insect with hard wing cases; another insect word with the same first sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甲虫」，是另一个以同一音开头的昆虫词。

entries.definition: The plural of bee, with a voiced ending.
entries.definitionCN: bee 的复数形式，词尾读作浊音。

entries.definition: A thin-bodied stinging insect that does not make honey.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄蜂」，体型细长、会蜇人但不酿蜜。

entries.definition: A large wasp with a painful sting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大黄蜂」，体型大、蜇人很痛。

entries.definition: The specific bee kept for honey; it names the first sense more exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜜蜂」，专指用来产蜜的蜂，比 bee 更精确。

entries.definition: A small social insect that lives in colonies, like the bee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蚂蚁」，与蜜蜂一样是群居昆虫。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Germanic family, the real compounds, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的日耳曼语词族、真实复合词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English beo meant this insect, and Dutch bij and German Biene still do.
normal.cn: 古英语 beo 就指这种昆虫，荷兰语 bij 和德语 Biene 至今仍如此。

normal.en: Picture the pollen baskets on the back legs: that is the honey-making bee.
normal.cn: 想象后腿上的花粉篮，那就是酿蜜的蜜蜂。

normal.en: The bee in spelling bee is not an insect but an old word for a gathering.
normal.cn: spelling bee 里的 bee 不是虫子，而是旧时表示「聚会」的词。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with queen, worker, sting and hive.
normal.cn: 它常与 queen、worker、sting、hive 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-e-e: three letters with two e's side by side, like two bees on a flower.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-e，三个字母里两个 e 并排，像花上并排的两只蜂。

abstract.en: See a bee lift off, dropping a little pollen behind it: that is the act of collecting.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜂起飞，身后洒下一点花粉，那就是「采集」的动作。

abstract.en: Lay the picture of a gathering over the insect picture, and spelling bee follows naturally.
abstract.cn: 把「聚在一起」的画面叠到昆虫画面上，拼字比赛就顺理成章。

abstract.en: Say the long vowel first, then let the flower bring the insect back.
abstract.cn: 先读出那个长元音，再让花的画面把昆虫带回来。

examples.en: A bee landed on the yellow flower.
examples.cn: 一只蜜蜂落在黄花上。

examples.en: Bees live together in a hive.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂一起住在蜂巢里。

examples.en: She won the school spelling bee.
examples.cn: 她在学校的拼字比赛中获胜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比」——它比谁都勤快，天天采蜜：蜜蜂

root: bee 来自古英语 beo，是日耳曼语里对酿蜜蜂的古老称呼，荷兰语 bij 与德语 Biene 都与它同源。近代英语里 bee 还指邻里聚在一起干活的聚会，这一用法今天主要保存在 spelling bee 中。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bee grow from one picture: a small insect that never stops moving from flower to flower.
sensesIntro.cn: bee 的四个义项都从同一幅画面生长出来：一只从一朵花飞向另一朵花、从不停歇的小虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bee carrying two balls of pollen on its back legs
core.cn: 核心意象：一只后腿挂着两团花粉的蜜蜂

branches.en: THE INSECT: the honey-making bee is the sense every other use rests on.
branches.cn: 昆虫线：酿蜜的蜜蜂是其他用法所依靠的义项。

branches.en: THE GROUP: wasps and other relatives widen the name to a whole family of stinging insects.
branches.cn: 同类线：黄蜂等近亲把这个名字扩展到一整类会蜇人的昆虫。

branches.en: THE GATHERING: the old sense of neighbours meeting survives inside spelling bee.
branches.cn: 聚会线：邻里相聚的旧义保存在拼字比赛这个词组里。

branches.en: THE WORKER: a bee never rests, so the picture also names a busy person.
branches.cn: 勤劳线：蜜蜂从不停歇，于是这幅画也用来指忙碌的人。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: one old word for a gathering and one word for an insect ended up in the same three letters.
branches.cn: 合流线：一个表示聚会的旧词和一个表示昆虫的词，最后落在同样的三个字母上。

intro.en: Bee is a base noun; the listed parts are real compounds and inflections built on it.
intro.cn: bee 是基础名词，下面列出的是由它构成的真实复合词与屈折形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin apis is recorded for the bee, but English took the word from Germanic, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语确有 apis 表示蜜蜂，但英语这个词来自日耳曼语，并非借自拉丁语。

items.example: A bee flew over the garden.

items.exampleCN: 它把 bee 变成 bees。
它与 bee 构成 beehive。
它与 bee 构成 beekeeper。
它与 bee 构成 beeswax。

items.meaning: a sharp wound from an insect
items.example: A bee sting can hurt for a day.
The queen bee stays in the hive.

items.meaning: the act of writing letters in order
items.exampleCN: 它与 bee 构成拼字比赛。

definition_zh: 燃烧；烧毁；烧伤、烫伤；发烫、灼热
definition_en: to be on fire, to destroy or damage something with fire or heat, to injure the skin with heat, or to feel very hot
core_image: 橙色火苗舔着一块木头，木头发红发黑
scene: 炉火太旺，锅底的一层油忽然烧了起来。 The oil in the pan began to burn.
sceneCN: 这里 burn 是「燃烧」（第 1 个义项：着火、烧起来）；句意为炉火太旺，锅底的那层油忽然烧了起来。

pos.zh: 动词：燃烧；烧毁；灼伤；发烫

derivatives.zh: 由 burn 加 -er 构成，义为「燃烧器；炉头」

senses.title: To be on fire
senses.definition: to be on fire, or to produce flames and heat
senses.definitionCN: 着火，或产生火焰与热量
senses.example: The oil in the pan began to burn.
senses.exampleCN: 锅底的那层油开始烧了起来。
senses.why: Old English had two verbs, beornan for something already on fire and bærnan for setting it alight.
senses.whyCN: 古英语有两个动词：beornan 指某物自己在烧，bærnan 指点火把它烧起来。

senses.title: To destroy with fire
senses.definition: to destroy or damage something by fire or great heat
senses.definitionCN: 用火或高温毁坏、损坏某物
senses.example: The fire burned down the old barn.
senses.exampleCN: 大火把旧谷仓烧毁了。
senses.why: When fire takes a whole object, the burning ends in nothing, so the verb came to mean destroying as well.
senses.whyCN: 当火吞掉整件东西，燃烧的结局就是化为乌有，于是这个动词也指毁掉。

senses.title: To injure the skin with heat
senses.definition: to hurt or damage the skin with fire, heat or a hot liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用火、高温或热液伤害皮肤
senses.example: She burned her hand on the hot pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手被热锅烫伤了。
senses.why: The same heat that feeds a flame also injures flesh, so the verb covers the harm done to a body.
senses.whyCN: 供养火焰的那份热也会伤到皮肉，所以这个动词也指身体受到的伤害。

senses.title: To feel very hot
senses.definition: to feel very hot, or to give out a strong heat, often used of skin or the sun
senses.definitionCN: 感到极热，或散发出强烈的热，常用于皮肤或太阳
senses.example: His forehead was burning with fever.
senses.exampleCN: 他发着烧，额头滚烫。
senses.why: A body on fire and a body with fever feel the same, so the word also describes heat inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 着火的物体和发烧的身体感觉相同，所以这个词也用来形容人体内的热度。

intro.en: Burn comes from two old verbs, one for being on fire and one for setting fire, which merged into a single word.
intro.cn: burn 来自两个古动词，一个指自己着火，一个指点火，二者后来合成一个词。

items.en: Beornan meant to be on fire, used of the thing that burns.
items.cn: beornan 意为正在着火，用于燃烧的那件东西。

items.en: Baernan meant to set something on fire, used of the person who lights it.
items.cn: baernan 意为点燃某物，用于点火的人。

items.en: German brennen and Dutch branden keep both senses in one verb.
items.cn: 德语 brennen 与荷兰语 branden 把一个动词的两种用法都保留下来。

items.en: The two verbs merged into burn, and burnt or burned served as the past form.
items.cn: 两个动词合并为 burn，过去式用 burnt 或 burned。

items.en: Today burn covers fire, destruction, injury and the heat of fever.
items.cn: 今天 burn 覆盖着火、烧毁、灼伤与发烧的热度。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about fire and heat.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与火、热有关的词。

normal.en: German brennen and Dutch branden are close cousins of the same verb.

normal.en: The heat that feeds a flame also hurts skin, so burn means both.

abstract.cn: 想象一簇橙色火苗舔着一块木头，直到木头变黑：这簇火就是 burn。

abstract.en: Move that heat onto a hand and the same picture becomes a painful injury.
abstract.cn: 把这股热移到手背上，同一幅画面就变成疼痛的伤。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the orange flame bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那簇橙色火苗把意思带回来。

root: burn 来自两个古英语动词：beornan 指某物自己在烧，bærnan 指点火把它烧起来，二者在中古英语合并为 burn，与德语 brennen、荷兰语 branden 同源。这个词从着火扩展到烧毁与灼伤；因为发烧的身体和着火的物体感觉相似，它又用来形容体内的高热。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of burn rest on one picture: an orange flame feeding on something until it changes.
sensesIntro.cn: burn 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：一簇橙色火苗正在吞噬某物，直到它改变模样。

core.cn: 核心意象：橙色火苗舔着木头，直到木头变黑

branches.cn: 火焰线：正在着火是最字面的第一个义项。

branches.en: THE RUIN: fire that takes a whole object destroys it.
branches.cn: 毁坏线：火吞掉整件东西，就把它毁掉。

branches.en: THE WOUND: the same heat injures flesh.
branches.cn: 伤口线：同样的热会伤到皮肉。

branches.en: THE FEVER: heat inside a body feels like a flame.
branches.cn: 高热线：体内的热感觉像火焰。

branches.en: THE LOSS: destruction and injury both leave something gone.
branches.cn: 损失线：毁坏与灼伤都会留下缺损。

definition_zh: 更晚的；后来的；以后
definition_en: at a time after the present or after a stated moment; the comparative of late
core_image: 日历上今天这一页被翻过去，手指停在后面那一页
scene: 会议原定上午结束，讨论却一直拖到下午。 The decision was postponed to a later date.
sceneCN: 这里是「更晚的、以后的」（第 1 个义项：形容词，指时间在现在或某一时点之后）；句意为决定被推迟到更晚的日期。图中可辨识物件：日历、被翻过的一页、会议桌。

derivatives.zh: 由 late 的最高级构成，义为「最新的；最近的」
与 late 同源的比较形式，义为「后者的；较后的」
由 late 与 comer 复合，义为「迟到者；后来者」

senses.title: At a time after the present or a stated moment
senses.definition: happening or existing at a time after now or after a moment already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 发生在现在或已提到的某一时点之后
senses.example: The decision was postponed to a later date.
senses.exampleCN: 决定被推迟到更晚的日期。
senses.why: Later is simply the comparative of late: two points on a line, and this one sits further to the right.
senses.whyCN: later 就是 late 的比较级：时间线上有两个点，这个词指更靠后的那一个。

senses.title: Afterwards, at some future time
senses.definition: at a time in the future, especially after something else has happened
senses.definitionCN: 在将来的某个时间，尤指在另一件事之后
senses.example: We can discuss the details later.
senses.exampleCN: 细节我们可以以后再谈。
senses.why: The adjective's comparison turns into an adverb of time, so later can stand alone as 'afterwards' without naming a second point.
senses.whyCN: 形容词的比较义转为时间副词，于是 later 可以独立表示「后来」，不必再点出第二个时点。

intro.en: Later is the comparative of late, an Old English adjective for slow and tardy that shifted its centre to time.
intro.cn: later 是 late 的比较级；late 是古英语中表示「慢、迟」的形容词，后来重心转到时间上。

items.en: Læt meant slow, sluggish or tardy, describing a person or thing that moves behind time.
items.cn: læt 意为慢的、迟缓的、迟到的，描述落在时间后面的 人或物。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family that also gives German lass and the idea of letting go.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，同族还包括德语 lass 以及「放开」的概念。

items.en: The old comparative ending -ra produced lætra, the ancestor of later.
items.cn: 古老的比较级词尾 -ra 造出 lætra，即 later 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English later is fixed as the comparative of late and begins to work as an adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语中 later 固定为 late 的比较级，并开始作副词使用。

items.en: Modern English adds the fixed phrases later on and sooner or later.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 later on 与 sooner or later 这类固定短语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same late family; the near-meaning group gathers words for a time that comes after.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 late 词族的各种形式；近义组收表示「之后」的时间词。

abstract.en: Later always needs an anchor: now, or an event just mentioned.

abstract.en: A word for slow became a word for late, and then for the future.

senses.title: To find something new
senses.definition: to find a place, thing or animal that nobody knew before
senses.definitionCN: 发现以前没人知道的地方、东西或动物
senses.example: Columbus discovered a new continent in 1492.
senses.exampleCN: 哥伦布于1492年发现了一片新大陆。
senses.why: The old sense of cover meant to hide; dis- removes the cover, and what was hidden shows itself.
senses.whyCN: cover 的旧义是「遮盖」，dis- 把盖子揭开，藏起来的东西便显露出来。

senses.title: To learn or notice a fact
senses.definition: to find out a fact or to notice something
senses.definitionCN: 得知某个事实或注意到某事
senses.example: She discovered a talent for drawing in art class.
senses.exampleCN: 她在美术课上发现了自己的绘画天赋。
senses.why: Facts hide too; lifting their cover is learning them.
senses.whyCN: 事实也会藏起来，掀开它的「盖子」就是了解它。

intro.en: Discover is cover plus dis-: to un-cover.

items.en: Latin cooperire meant to cover completely, from co- (together) and operire (to close).

items.en: Old French covrir meant to cover.

items.en: The prefix dis- built discover, at first meaning to reveal or tell.

items.en: The Age of Exploration fixed the sense of finding unknown lands.
items.cn: 大航海时代确立了「发现未知之地」的义项。

definition_zh: 没有什么；没有东西；无关紧要的事；零
definition_en: not anything at all; something too small to matter; and a score of zero in a game
core_image: 抽屉拉开，里面空空的，只有一层薄灰在光里浮动
scene: 抽屉被整个拉开，里面空空的，只有一层薄灰在光里浮动。 The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
sceneCN: 这里是「没有什么、没有东西」（第 1 个义项：一样东西都不存在），句意为抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。图中可辨识物件：拉开的抽屉、薄灰、窗光。

derivatives.zh: 由 nothing 加 -ness（性质、状态）构成，义为「虚无；空无」
由 good for nothing 固定成词，义为「无用的人」

senses.title: Not anything at all
senses.definition: not a single thing, used when absolutely nothing exists, happens or is present
senses.definitionCN: 一样东西也没有，用于表示完全不存在、不发生或不在场
senses.example: The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。
senses.why: Old English joined nān, meaning not one, to þing, meaning thing, so the word literally says not one thing and still carries that flat emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 古英语把表示「一个也不」的 nān 与表示「东西」的 þing 拼在一起，所以这个词字面上说的是「一样东西也没有」，至今仍带着那种空荡。

senses.title: Something too small or unimportant to matter
senses.titleCN: 无关紧要的事；微不足道的东西
senses.definition: a person or thing of no importance, or a remark or event that matters very little
senses.definitionCN: 不重要的人或事，或价值极小的言论与事件
senses.example: They argued for an hour over nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为一件无关紧要的事争了一个小时。
senses.why: If a thing is nothing, it is not worth counting, so the word easily shifts from absence to worthlessness, especially when people want to dismiss a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事是 nothing，就等于不值得计算，于是这个词很容易从「不存在」转到「不值得」，尤其是在人们想打发一句抱怨的时候。

senses.title: A score of zero in a game
senses.definition: zero as a score, especially in sports and games
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或游戏中的零分
senses.example: The match ended three to nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛以三比零结束。
senses.why: A team with no runs has literally scored nothing, so the word for no thing became the name of the zero on the scoreboard.
senses.whyCN: 一支没有得分的队，字面上就是「什么也没得到」，于是表示「无物」的词成了记分牌上那个零的名称。

intro.en: Nothing is a native English compound of a negative word for not one and the noun for thing, and it contracted into a single pronoun in Old English.
intro.cn: nothing 是英语本土的复合词，由一个表示「一个也不」的否定词与表示「东西」的名词组成，在古英语里就已缩合成一个代词。

items.en: Nān was ne plus ān, not one, and it denied even a single item rather than merely denying a quality.
items.cn: nān 是 ne 加 ān，意为「一个也不」，它连单独一样东西都否定，而不只是否定某种性质。

items.en: Þing meant a thing, a matter or an assembly, and it supplied the noun half of the compound.
items.cn: þing 意为东西、事情或议事会，为这个复合词提供了名词那一半。

items.en: The two words were written together as nānþing and behaved as a single pronoun meaning no thing at all.
items.cn: 两个词被写在一起作 nānþing，像一个代词那样使用，意为「一样东西也没有」。

items.en: Middle English respelled the compound with not and thing, matching the shortened negator, and the old nān disappeared from it.
items.cn: 中古英语用 not 与 thing 重拼这个复合词，与缩短的否定词保持一致，旧的 nān 从中消失。

items.en: Modern English keeps nothing as a pronoun and a noun, and fixed phrases such as nothing but and for nothing carry the old emptiness into idiom.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nothing 兼作代词与名词，nothing but、for nothing 这类固定说法把古老的「空」带进了成语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other thing-pronouns built on the same pattern; the near-meaning group collects the words English uses for none and zero.
note.cn: 形近组收按同一模式造出的其他 thing 代词；近义组收英语里表示「无」与「零」的词。

entries.definition: A pronoun for any thing at all, built on the same thing element.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「任何东西」的代词，用了同一个 thing 成分。

entries.definition: A pronoun for one unspecified thing, the positive partner of nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某个不指定东西的代词，是 nothing 的肯定对应词。

entries.definition: The noun inside nothing, meaning an object, matter or event.
entries.definitionCN: nothing 里的那个名词，意为物体、事情或事件。

entries.definition: Not one, or not any, used when a quantity is zero.
entries.definitionCN: 一个也不、任何也不，用于数量为零时。

entries.definition: The number that stands for no quantity at all.
entries.definitionCN: 表示完全没有数量的那个数字。

entries.definition: Nothing, especially a zero score in sports and records.
entries.definitionCN: 无，尤指体育与记录中的零分。

normalIntro.en: The word is not one plus thing, and its later senses keep asking what counts as a thing worth having.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一个也没有」加「东西」，它后来的义项一直在追问：什么才算值得拥有的东西。

normal.en: Nothing is nān plus þing: not one thing, so the word itself explains its own emptiness.
normal.cn: nothing 是 nān 加 þing：一样东西也没有，词本身就把自己的空说清楚了。

normal.en: The same nān is behind no and none, which is why all three refuse a quantity.
normal.cn: 同一个 nān 也藏在 no 与 none 后面，所以这三者都在拒绝某个数量。

normal.en: Middle English respelled the compound with not, linking nothing to the history of not.
normal.cn: 中古英语用 not 重拼这个复合词，把 nothing 与 not 的历史连在一起。

normal.en: Nothing but means only, because everything else has been excluded.
normal.cn: nothing but 意为「只有」，因为其余的一切都被排除掉了。

normal.en: For nothing means either free or wasted, and both say that no payment or result came back.
normal.cn: for nothing 既可以是「免费」，也可以是「白费」，两者都说没有回报或没有结果。

abstract.en: A word made of not one and thing turns absence into a noun, so English can talk about emptiness as if it were an object.
abstract.cn: 一个由「一个也不」和「东西」构成的词，把缺席变成了名词，于是英语能像谈论物件一样谈论空。

abstract.en: When nothing also means unimportant, the language quietly ranks existence by worth.
abstract.cn: 当 nothing 也指「不重要」，语言就在悄悄按价值给存在排位。

abstract.en: On a scoreboard nothing is a number, which shows how easily a word for absence can be counted.
abstract.cn: 在记分牌上 nothing 是一个数字，这说明表示「无」的词多么容易被计数。

examples.en: The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
examples.cn: 抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。

examples.en: They argued for an hour over nothing.
examples.cn: 他们为一件无关紧要的事争了一个小时。

examples.en: The match ended three to nothing.
examples.cn: 比赛以三比零结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那辛」——拉开抽屉，里面空空如也，什么也没有；nothing 就是没有什么。

root: 古英语 nān（ne 加 ān，一个也不）与 þing（东西）合成 nānþing，中古英语重拼为 nothing；与 not 同出这一否定词源，英语中没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not one thing; it then extends to what is not worth counting and to the zero on a scoreboard.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一样东西也没有」；义项由此扩展到不值得计算的东西，以及记分牌上的零。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open drawer that is completely empty except for a thin layer of dust.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉开的抽屉空空如也，只有一层薄灰。

branches.en: an empty drawer holding only dust
branches.cn: 空抽屉里只有一层灰

branches.en: a hand patting a pocket with no keys in it
branches.cn: 手拍口袋，里面没有钥匙

branches.en: a quarrel over something too small to name
branches.cn: 为一件小得叫不出名字的事争吵

branches.en: a scoreboard still blank after the first half
branches.cn: 半场过后记分牌上仍是空白

branches.en: a team walking off with a zero beside its name
branches.cn: 球队离场，名字旁边是一个零

intro.en: The word joins an Old English negative for not one to the noun for thing, and English built its abstract noun and its dismissive compound on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语表示「一个也不」的否定词接到表示「东西」的名词上，英语又在这个底座上造出抽象名词和表示轻蔑的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Nothing has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin nihil is built from ne and hilum, not a whit, a different formation, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: nothing 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语用「nihil」表示「无」，它由「ne」与「hilum」（一点点）构成，构词方式不同，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 控制；管理；操纵；（遥控器等的）控制器
definition_en: to make someone or something do what you want, or the power to do this
core_image: 手握方向盘或遥控器的那只手
scene: 遥控赛车在操场上飞驰，他指哪儿车去哪儿。 Learn to control your temper when playing games.
sceneCN: 这里 control 是「控制」（第 1 个义项：约束自己的行为情绪）；句意是打游戏时学会控制脾气。

derivatives.zh: 由 control 加 -er 构成，义为「控制器；管理员」
由 control 加 -able 构成，义为「可控的」
由 un- 加 controllable 构成，义为「无法控制的」

senses.title: To direct or limit something
senses.definition: to make something behave the way you want
senses.definitionCN: 让事物按你的意愿运作
senses.example: Control your speed on the downhill.
senses.exampleCN: 下坡时控制好车速。
senses.why: The Medieval Latin phrase contra rotulum meant a counter-roll used to check records: checking became ruling.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 contra rotulum 指用于核对的副本卷册，「核对」引申为「掌控」。

senses.title: To hold back feelings
senses.definition: to stop yourself from showing anger, fear or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 克制怒气、恐惧或兴奋
senses.example: He could not control his laughter in class.
senses.exampleCN: 他在课上忍不住笑出声来。
senses.why: Rules that govern machines can also govern feelings.
senses.whyCN: 管机器的规矩同样能管住情绪。

senses.title: The power to direct something
senses.definition: the ability or right to decide how something works
senses.definitionCN: 支配事物运作的能力或权力
senses.example: The coach has full control of the training plan.
senses.exampleCN: 教练全权掌握训练计划。
senses.why: The act of ruling becomes the power itself.
senses.whyCN: 「掌控」的动作沉淀为「权力」本身。

senses.title: A device that operates a machine
senses.definition: a tool or set of buttons used to work a machine
senses.definitionCN: 操控机器的工具或按键组
senses.example: The game control fits small hands well.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏手柄很适合小手。
senses.why: The power sits in your hands, so the tool took the name.
senses.whyCN: 权力握在手里，操控工具便借用了这个名字。

intro.en: Control began with a second scroll used to check the first.
intro.cn: control 起于「用副本卷册核对正本」。

items.en: Medieval Latin contrarotulus meant a counter-roll, a copy used for checking accounts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus 指核对账目用的副本卷册。

items.en: Old French controle meant checking against a register.
items.cn: 古法语 controle 指对照登记册核查。

items.en: Middle English controle first meant official checking of accounts.
items.cn: 中古英语 controle 起初指对账目的官方核查。

items.en: Middle English controle later meant restraining and commanding people.
items.cn: 中古英语 controle 后来指约束与指挥。

items.en: Modern English control added machines, feelings and devices.
items.cn: 现代英语 control 又覆盖机器、情绪与控制器。

note.en: The first group collects words close in spelling; the second collects words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近的词，第二组收近义词。

entries.definition: A device or person that controls.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「控制器；管理员」，与 control 同根。

entries.definition: Able to be controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可控的」，同根派生词。

entries.definition: Not an English word; beware of the spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 并非英语单词，注意与 control 区分拼写。

entries.definition: A clear difference.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「对比」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To run or handle something well.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理；设法做到」。

entries.definition: To make a machine work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「操作」，多指机器。

entries.definition: To order or direct with authority.

normalIntro.en: Remember control through checking rolls and steady hands.
normalIntro.cn: 从「核对卷册」与「稳住的手」记 control。

normal.en: control once meant a copy roll for checking.
normal.cn: control 曾指用于核对的副本卷册。

normal.en: under control means safe and managed.
normal.cn: under control 表示在掌控之中。

normal.en: A remote control works from far away.
normal.cn: 遥控器能远距离操作。

normal.en: The double l appears in controlled and controlling.
normal.cn: controlled 与 controlling 中 l 要双写。

normal.en: control and contrast differ in the middle letters.
normal.cn: control 与 contrast 中间字母不同。

abstract.en: Grip the steering wheel of a bumper car.
abstract.cn: 紧握碰碰车的方向盘。

abstract.en: Breathe slowly to cool a hot temper.
abstract.cn: 深呼吸让火气降温。

abstract.en: See a single button steer a whole toy car.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按键指挥整辆玩具车。

examples.en: Keep the ball under control during the dribble.
examples.cn: 运球时把球控制在自己脚下。

examples.en: She controlled her nerves before the piano contest.
examples.cn: 钢琴比赛前她控制住了紧张情绪。

examples.en: The pilot kept full control of the plane in the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴中飞行员牢牢掌控着飞机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯抽喽」——肯上手就能抽着缰绳喽，control 就是控制。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 contra（相对）+ rotulus（卷册）→ contrarotulus（核对用的副本）→ 古法语 controle（核查）→ 中古英语 controle → 现代英语 control；同族词有 controller（控制器）、controllable（可控的）、roll（卷册）。

sensesIntro.en: Control runs from checking records to ruling, restraining and buttons in hand.
sensesIntro.cn: control 从「核对」长成掌管、克制与手中的按键。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand that decides what happens next
core.cn: 核心意象：决定下一步的稳稳的手

branches.en: Speed held steady downhill
branches.cn: 下坡时被稳住的车速

branches.en: Laughter held back in class
branches.cn: 课上被憋住的笑声

branches.en: The coach's training plan
branches.cn: 教练的训练计划权

branches.en: A remote in small hands
branches.cn: 小手中的遥控器

branches.en: Self-control in a tight match
branches.cn: 胶着比赛中的自控力

intro.en: Control keeps a family of ruling and checking words.
intro.cn: control 围绕「掌管与核对」形成词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root contra rotulus means a counter-roll for checking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 contra rotulus 意为核对用的副本卷册。

items.example: The drone is easy controllable for beginners.
items.exampleCN: 无人机对新手来说很容易操控。
自控力对考试很有帮助。
